Filed rather than fixed because the honest options are a signature that cannot express the empty case or a sentinel that changes what a caller reads, and neither is worth choosing without a second caller to design against.
## Surfaced by the #789 round 31 Playwright e2e lane (2026-09-02)

The three defects this lane found were fixed in-round
([decisions § 904](../architecture/decisions.md) / [§ 905](../architecture/decisions.md)).
These are what is left: two more instances of the same `functions.invoke`
envelope shape that no spec of this lane proves wrong today, one honest
untestable, and one narrow undo bug.

- [x] **`startDonationCheckout` and `edgeFunctionExport` still rethrow the raw `FunctionsHttpError`.** Both were left alone because neither currently PUTS the message in front of a person — the fundraiser page catches and shows the fixed `fundraiser.donateFailed`, and the legacy export path's message reaches a toast that reads as a generic failure either way. So nothing leaks the internal sentence there, and there was no defect for a spec to prove. What both DO lose is the refusal itself: `donations-checkout` can answer `fundraiser_closed` / `host_cannot_take_payment`, and a donor told only "could not start the donation" cannot tell "this fundraiser has ended" from "try again in a minute". `core/edge_function_error.ts` now exists, so closing this is an unwrap plus a code→copy map on each, exactly the shape the event-register path took. Do it when either surface next gets worked on rather than as a sweep — each needs its own copy decisions and its own i18n keys. Both closed 2026-09-02 — [decisions § 982](../architecture/decisions.md) (donation) and [§ 983](../architecture/decisions.md) (export). Two corrections to the filing: the code is `owner_cannot_take_payment`, not `host_cannot_take_payment` (a map written from this text would have silently never matched, which is now guarded), and the export path did NOT merely reach a generic toast — `settingsAccount.exportFailed` interpolates `{error}`, so "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code" was rendered to the subject verbatim.
- [x] **`settings/integrations-connected.spec.ts`'s "Disconnect Strava" test cannot pass against a local stack, and nothing says so.** Disconnect goes through the `strava-import` Edge Function on purpose (it revokes at Strava's end and wipes the vault rows rather than doing a bare DELETE), so it needs the Strava env CI's functions host carries and the local one does not. Reproduced against `origin/main` with this lane's source changes reverted, so it is environmental and not a regression — but a spec that is red on every developer's machine and green on CI trains people to ignore reds. Either skip it when the env is absent (the way `paywall-wire.spec.ts` auto-skips on `BYPASS_PAYWALL`) or say so in `test_inventory.md`; a silent permanent red is the worst of the three options. **Closed 2026-09-02 by taking the second option, because the first rests on a false premise.** Measured: the disconnect path needs NO Strava credentials (`plantIntegration` writes no tokens, so `handleDisconnect` resolves an empty access token and skips the deauthorize outright), and CI's `e2e-web` job carries none either — it runs `supabase start` and never `functions serve --env-file`, and no `apps/backend/supabase/.env` is committed — so an env-keyed skip would have skipped on CI too and deleted the coverage. The real local failure is the ONE edge-runtime container shared across every worktree: it is bind-mounted at the tree it was started from, and once that directory is replaced under it every invoke answers `{"code":"BOOT_ERROR"}` / 503 with `failed to determine entrypoint` in its log — reproduced against strava-import, race-listings-sync and race-results-import together. That is not per-spec and no per-spec skip can express it, so the cause is written into the spec header and `test_inventory.md` instead.
- [x] **A deferred wear-log delete whose commit later fails repaints a stale list into whichever gear modal is open.** `removeWearLog` in `/settings/gear` captures `before = wearLogs` and restores it on undo OR on a commit failure. Undo is immediate and safe; the commit runs when the window closes, by which time the runner may have closed that modal and opened another pair's, and `restore` then writes gear X's observations into gear Y's open modal. A reload fixes it and nothing is destroyed (the row survives, which is the fail-safe direction), so this is cosmetic — but it is the only adopter of the undo queue and the same shape will be wrong in a worse place when the second one arrives. The durable fix is for `restore` to be a no-op when the list it snapshotted is no longer the one on screen, which means the callback needs to know what it is restoring INTO. Closed 2026-09-02 — [decisions § 984](../architecture/decisions.md). The queue's contract is untouched, so nothing is owed on the Dart side. Reference identity turned out to be the wrong test (`wearLogs` is a `$state` array, so the value read back is a proxy, not the array assigned); an explicit epoch bumped by a single `setWearLogs` is, and a source guard fails the PR on any write that bypasses it.
## Surfaced by the #789 round 31 mobile lane (2026-09-02)

The three boxes this lane could close outright are ticked above — the two
`off_route_alert` halves and the `e164` hyphen family, each fixed on both sides
of its parity pair together
([decisions §§ 929-930](../architecture/decisions.md) and
[§ 933](../architecture/decisions.md)). Nine more pairs were registered after
being measured, four of them carrying live divergences that were fixed
([§ 931](../architecture/decisions.md)). What follows is what the lane found and
did not take.

- [x] **`public.runs` has no `distance_m >= 0` or `duration_s >= 0` CHECK, and at least one client was written believing it did.** Closed 2026-09-02 ([decisions § 939](../architecture/decisions.md)): migration `20270704000001` adds `runs_distance_m_check`, `runs_duration_s_check` and `runs_elevation_gain_m_check`, each `NOT VALID` then validated, behind a predicate-scoped repair that matches nothing on a healthy database. The bound is NOT the `>= 0` the box asked for: `'NaN'::numeric >= 0` is true, so each numeric term names NaN explicitly and `elevation_gain_m` names Infinity too. Two exploits measured over PostgREST with an ordinary password-grant JWT before the fix — a NaN run took rank 1 of every distance challenge its author had joined, and a negative `duration_s` became the account 5k best. Not registered in `check_constraint_unions.mjs`: its coverage rule reads set-shaped `check (col in (…))` only and an entry for a range column fails it. Pinned by `runs_physical_quantity_bounds_test.sql` (16 assertions, three mutations killed). Original entry: The CSV importer passed a negative distance straight through under a comment naming "the DB CHECK (distance_m >= 0, duration_s >= 0)" as the source of truth. Those CHECKs are on `event_results` and `gym_workouts`; `runs.distance_m` is `numeric(10, 2) not null` with no constraint, and `duration_s` is a bare `integer not null`. The client half is closed ([decisions § 934](../architecture/decisions.md)) but the column is still the wrong shape: `numeric` accepts `NaN` and `Infinity` as well as negatives, so any writer that gets it wrong — a future importer, a hand-run SQL fix, a third-party integration — silently poisons every aggregate that sums the column. Not taken in-round because `apps/backend/` belongs to no lane this round AND because these are populated prod tables: the change is a `NOT VALID` add plus a separate `VALIDATE`, per `docs/backend/migration_locks.md`, and it needs a backfill decision for any row already out of range. Add `runs_distance_m_check` and `runs_duration_s_check` together, and register the column in `check_constraint_unions.mjs`'s `PAIRS` with an empty `clients` list and a note (no client enumerates a range).
- [x] **`classifyStravaRow` and `indexHeader` are web-only, and the mobile analogue does not share the defect — so the filed entry above needs a web owner, not a mobile one.** Determined this round: `apps/web/src/lib/integrations/strava-zip-*.ts` has no Dart counterpart, because mobile's Strava path (`strava_importer.dart`) reads the API rather than a bulk-export ZIP, and mobile's own CSV importer resolves columns to a nullable index with an explicit missing-required-columns failure rather than to `-1`. So the `row[-1] → undefined → 'import'` chain exists on web alone. The mobile lane closed the equivalent class where it does exist (an unvalidated `activity_type` reaching a CHECK-constrained column, § 934), but the web entry stands untouched and unticked. Closed 2026-09-03 — [decisions § 1042](../architecture/decisions.md). **The filing was stale in its own last sentence**: the entry above is `- [x]`, closed by § 979 on 2026-09-02. Its ownership claim was right and the chain WAS still live — on three other columns. `Activity Date` unresolved stamped every row with the moment of the import (five years of history on today, corrupting streaks, PR brackets, the calendar and training load); `Moving Time` gave every run a zero duration; neither distance column resolved gave every run zero distance. All six required columns are now refused at the header, naming whichever are missing, with the distance requirement satisfied by either block; and a single row whose date cell cannot be parsed is refused and reported in the `ImportFailureReport` rather than filed under today. Pinned by `strava_zip_required_columns.test.ts` — executable on `indexHeader`'s -1 premise, source-level on the guard, both mutation-tested.
- [x] **Every mobile deploy gate that reads a value out of the settings bag inherits the `cycle_plan` shape, and nothing sweeps for it.** `cycle_plan` failed differently on each platform for a malformed date because `parseInt` yields NaN where `int.parse` throws; fixed there ([decisions § 934](../architecture/decisions.md) records the class, § 931 the pair). The settings bag is jsonb, so every `int.parse` / `double.parse` / `DateTime.parse` reached from a value another client wrote has the same exposure, and the non-throwing `tryParse` family has the mirror-image one — it accepts the literals `NaN` and `Infinity`, which is what put a non-finite coordinate into a `Waypoint` on all four import formats. A source-level guard in the mobile suite (no bare `int.parse` / `double.parse` on a settings-bag or file-parsed value; every `double.tryParse` result checked for `isFinite` before it reaches a model) would turn a class the lane found three instances of into one that cannot recur. Filed rather than written because the guard needs an allowlist for the many legitimate in-repo parses and that list is the real work. Closed 2026-09-02 — [decisions § 1011](../architecture/decisions.md). **The filed class is empty**: exactly two call sites in the whole tree read a jsonb bag key and both were already handled. The class BESIDE it is real — `double.tryParse('NaN')` is NaN and `('1e400')` is Infinity, both non-null — and its allowlist is empty, so the guard was writable after all: 26 call sites, 23 already conforming. Three were not, one live on a shipped path (`geocoding.dart` built a `PlaceResult` from a Nominatim string with no finiteness and no range test; the MapTiler branch was exposed too, because `jsonDecode('1e400')` is Infinity).
- [x] **`csv_run_importer` now imports `preferences.dart` to reach the `ActivityType` vocabulary, which drags Material into a pure parser.** The import is `show ActivityType` and the alternative was worse — retyping the five values would create a second unregistered rail against `runs_activity_type_check`, which is the drift the constraint-union guard exists to prevent. But the vocabulary does not belong in a file that also holds `IconData` getters and a `SharedPreferences` cache. Moving the enum to `packages/core_models` (where `MetadataKeys` already lives, and which the importer already imports) would fix it properly, at the cost of touching every one of the eight `ActivityType.values` call sites plus the rail's registration in `check_constraint_unions.mjs`. Worth doing next time `core_models` is open. Closed 2026-09-02 — [decisions § 1013](../architecture/decisions.md).
- [x] **31 numeric columns in `public` carry no CHECK constraint at all, and two of them are rendered on a public map.** Closed 2026-09-03 ([decisions §§ 1046-1048](../architecture/decisions.md) + [§ 1051](../architecture/decisions.md)): migrations `20270705000001` (the eleven an anonymous spectator reads), `20270705000002` (the remaining NaN-capable ones), `20270705000003` and `20270705000004` (the integer family), each `NOT VALID` then validated with the pre-flight query set in its header. **The count is right for the subset it was about and wrong for the question it asks**: 31 is exactly the `numeric` / `double precision` set, name for name, but **79** numeric columns carried no single-column CHECK — the other 48 are integer-family, where NaN is unreachable at the type and the exposure is a nonsense sign. Both halves are closed. The ping exploit was measured, not reasoned about: from an ordinary account's own session one INSERT lands `lat = 'NaN'`, `lng = 'Infinity'`, `ele = 'NaN'`, `distance_m = 'NaN'`, `elapsed_s = -5`, `bpm = -40` on its own public run, and `anon` reads all six back. PostGIS raised a coercion NOTICE and clamped only its own derived point. **One column was not merely unbounded but unstatable**: `duplicate_plan_week` parked the tail of a plan at negative `week_index` to renumber it under a per-row unique constraint, so `week_index >= 0` broke the plan editor's duplicate-week button — closed by making that constraint `deferrable initially immediate` rather than by moving the hop into a positive scratch space (§ 1048). Five exemptions with reasons: four sequence-backed surrogate keys and the generated `segments.length_m`. The guard the entry asked for is rule 3 of `numeric_bounds_reject_nan_test.sql`, which now *requires* a bound rather than only grading the ones that exist, mutation-verified in both directions; and the entry's expectation that `check_constraint_unions.mjs` would need an entry does not apply — these are range bounds and its coverage rule reads `check (col in (…))` only. Original entry: The 2026-09-02 sweep that produced [decisions § 940](../architecture/decisions.md) closed every *existing* numeric bound that admitted NaN. It says nothing about a column that was never bounded, and the catalogue lists 31: `live_run_pings.lat` / `lng` / `ele` / `distance_m` and `race_pings.lat` / `lng` / `distance_m` (client-written, drawn on the anonymous spectator map — a NaN coordinate is a broken render for every viewer, not just the writer), `events.meet_lat` / `meet_lng`, `routes.distance_m` / `elevation_m`, `segments.length_m`, `global_segments.elevation_m`, `gym_workouts.volume_kg` (a derived cache, so its writer is a trigger — but nothing stops a direct write if a grant ever widens), `events.distance_m`, `event_checkpoints.position_m`, `route_markers.position_m`, `route_conditions.position_m`, `checkpoint_crossings.body_weight_pct`, `achievements.value_num`, `challenge_badges.final_value`, `monthly_funding.amount_received`, `plan_weeks.target_volume_m`, `plan_workouts.target_distance_m`, `training_plans.goal_distance_m` / `vdot`, and the five `fitness_snapshots` metrics. Not taken in the same round because each one needs its own answer — a latitude's range is not a distance's, `training_stress_bal` is legitimately negative, and a blanket finiteness constraint would be 31 constraints nobody had thought about individually. The two ping pairs are the ones to do first: they are the only entries on the list whose bad value is visible to someone other than its author. `numeric_bounds_reject_nan_test.sql` already holds the machinery — extending its rule 1 to *require* a bound rather than only grade the ones that exist is the shape of the guard once the columns are bounded.

- [x] **`npm run check:script-types` is RED on `test/789-r31-integration` itself, in three files no round-32 lane touched.** 14 errors across `scripts/check_toolchain_pins.mjs` (6), `scripts/check_toolchain_pins.test.mjs` (2) and `scripts/check_twin_claims.test.mjs` (6) — mostly `TS7006` implicit-`any` parameters on destructured helper arguments, plus three `TS2345`s where a `string | null` is passed to a parameter tsc has inferred as `null | undefined` because every call site in view passes a literal `null`. Confirmed **not** introduced by the sql lane: `git diff --name-only f20c19abd..HEAD` names no file under `scripts/`, and all three failing files are byte-identical to their base-commit versions. The `workflow-lint` job runs this guard, so the branch fails CI on it regardless of what the four lanes land. The fix is a JSDoc `@param` annotation on each destructured helper signature (the tree is `checkJs` + `strict` with no root `tsconfig.json`, so an un-annotated parameter has nothing to infer from) and widening the two toolchain-pin helper signatures to the `string | null` they are actually called with. Not taken by the sql lane because `scripts/` is outside every lane's owned paths this round and a concurrent edit there would conflict; handed to whoever integrates. **Closed — verified 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1056](../architecture/decisions.md)). Verified before acting rather than after: `npm run check:script-types` exits 0, and `git diff --stat main -- scripts/` from the round-35 wear branch is empty, so all three files are byte-identical to today's `main` and the guard is green on both. Round 33's `9bb122d64` (PR #851) fixed it in exactly the shape this entry prescribed — JSDoc `@param` annotations, 43 of them in `check_toolchain_pins.mjs` alone, with no tsconfig loosened. Nothing left to do.
## Surfaced by the #789 round 32 wrist lane (2026-09-02)

Four defects were fixed in-round across the three wrist tiers
([decisions §§ 944-948](../architecture/decisions.md)). What follows is what
this lane found and could not take, mostly because the artefact belongs in
`scripts/` or `.github/`, which no lane owned this round.

- [x] **`apps/watch_garmin/scripts/check_garmin_source.sh` is not wired into CI, so nothing runs the only guard the Garmin tier has.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 963](../architecture/decisions.md)). Its own `watch-garmin-source` job rather than a step in `watch-ios-locale-parity`: that job is already bundled and already annotates per step, so rule 2 would have been satisfied — but the job NAME is what a reader sees red in the checks list, and "watchOS source-level guards" going red for a Garmin defect is a name wrong about the TIER, which no per-step annotation corrects. Ungated, for the reason its sibling is. Two steps (the guard, then its own new 20-case mutation suite), each with an `::error::`, and the job named in the `CI gate` `needs:` list — both obligations were proved enforced by deleting them and watching `check_ci_diagnostics.mjs` refuse. Writing the suite found a live defect underneath the filing: `body_of` located declarations by SUBSTRING, so `function onTimerResetX` satisfied the claim that `onTimerReset` is overridden. Original filing below. It needs no Connect IQ SDK — bash + python3, the same shape as `apps/watch_ios/scripts/check_xcstrings_parity.sh`, which the `watch-ios-locale-parity` job already invokes the same way. Wiring is one step in an existing job (the `watch-ios-locale-parity` job is the natural host: it is already the "read the tier a compiler cannot reach" job) plus, if it becomes its own job, an entry in the `CI gate` aggregator's `needs:` list — a job the gate never waited for counts as no result, so an omitted line makes its red invisible rather than merely unlabelled. If it lands as a second guard inside an existing job, that job becomes a bundled one and every check step in it must print its own `::error::`. Until this is done the guard is a script: it passes today and nothing will notice the day it stops.
- [x] **The 99:00 live-pace ceiling and the 0.4 m/s walk gate are unregistered rails of `check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs`.** **CLOSED — verified 2026-09-02.** Round 33's guard lane ([decisions § 962](../architecture/decisions.md)) added both `CONSTANT_ROWS` entries and they run: `node scripts/check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs` reports `[OK] live-pace ceiling (s/km) = 5940 on 2 rails` and `[OK] live-pace walk gate (m/s) = 0.4 on 2 rails`. The filing's optional "if the chain is to be closed end to end" half is closed too, by three links rather than by one four-rail row: `apps/custom_watch/core/src/alerts.rs`'s `the_pace_band_ceiling_is_the_apps_own_live_pace_ceiling` asserts `PACE_BAND_MAX_S_PER_KM == grade_adjusted_pace::MAX_PACE_S_PER_KM`, and the `pace-band ceiling (s/km)` row pins that same firmware constant against the phone's `kWorkoutPaceMaxSecPerKm` (`= 5940 on 2 rails`). So Garmin `MAX_PACE_S` = firmware GAP = firmware alerts = phone, with every link read by something that fails. Original filing below. Both are now named constants on the Garmin side (`MAX_PACE_S`, `MIN_SPEED_MPS`), so `mcConst` can read them; the firmware holds `grade_adjusted_pace::MAX_PACE_S_PER_KM` and `MIN_SPEED_MPS`, whose doc comments both name the Garmin field as their source. Two new `CONSTANT_ROWS` entries — the ceiling across `RS_GAP` / `MC_GAP` (and, if the chain is to be closed end to end, `alerts::PACE_BAND_MAX_S_PER_KM` and the phone's `kWorkoutPaceMaxSecPerKm`, which are already a registered pair with each other), and the walk gate across `RS_GAP` / `MC_GAP`. Nothing is drifting today; the point is that a comment claiming a mirror is an instruction, not an enforcement.
- [x] **The phone-to-watch route-push envelope is read from one end only.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 966](../architecture/decisions.md)). Claim (7) of `check_watch_ios_source.mjs`, which already reads the opposite direction on the same session and is already CI-wired, so no new job. Measured before it was written: all three rails parse to the same five keys (`route_id`, `route_name`, `route_distance_m`, `route_lat`, `route_lng`), so the filing's "they agree today" is confirmed and this covers the future rather than a live defect. The comparison is pairwise over all three, in both directions, and each rail's rename fires it independently. The phone rail's parse deliberately reads its `args[…]` subscripts AND its repacked dictionary literal: `routeUserInfo` does both in one function, so a key it lifts and forwards under another name is a field dropped between two of its own lines. Original filing below. `WatchIngestBridge.routeUserInfo` (phone, Swift) writes `route_id` / `route_name` / `route_distance_m` / `route_lat` / `route_lng` into a `transferUserInfo` payload; `ArmedRoute.decode` (watch, Swift) reads exactly those five back; `apple_watch_route_bridge.dart` supplies them as method-channel args, a third rail. `check_watch_ios_source.mjs` reads the OPPOSITE direction on the same session (the `transferFile` run hand-off metadata) and does not touch this one, and `check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs` registers only the point-cap constant across those three files, not the key set. The three lists agree today — checked by hand this round — but a key renamed on one side is a route the runner arms on the phone that silently never reaches the wrist, which is precisely the failure the hand-off guard was written after. The claim is the same code: parse `payload["k"]` / `args["k"]` off each rail and compare the sets in both directions.
- [x] **No GAP rail has a minimum-RISE gate, only a minimum-run one, so sub-noise altitude reads as a wall on all four.** Closed 2026-09-02 — [decisions § 992](../architecture/decisions.md). Every arithmetic claim in the filing re-measured true (0.60 grade, factor 5.396; a 1 m step at 2.50). **The instrument is the window, and a rise threshold cannot work at any window**: the rise a real grade produces over the window scales with the window exactly as the noise does, so a 3 m gate zeroes every real grade under 60 % / 15 % / 10 % at a 5 / 20 / 30 m window while the GPS-altitude noise it aims at has a 1.95 / 3.82 / 4.61 m rise sigma and walks straight through — and on a CLEAN 3.3 % climb a 1 m gate read 19.5 % slow. `MIN_SEGMENT_M` is 20 m on all four rails: measured over an AR(1) altitude-error model, a flat 30-minute run reported GAP 47.9 % fast at 5 m against 26.8 % at 20 m under GPS altitude, and 9.0 % against 2.1 % at power-hike pace under a barometer, for a 2.5 % cost on the most oscillating realistic profile. **No `CONSTANT_ROWS` row is needed** — the `minimum segment before a grade sample is trusted (m)` row already binds all four, and `node scripts/check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs` reports it at 20 on 4 rails. `roadbook` shares the constant on three rails and moves with it. The Garmin rail is source-level only (no Connect IQ SDK on this machine). `MIN_SEGMENT_M = 5.0` gates the horizontal leg a grade sample is measured over; nothing gates the vertical. The repo's own barometric noise floor is `ELEVATION_GAIN_MIN_DELTA_M = 3` — a delta smaller than that is not treated as gain at all — and a 3 m rise over a 5 m run is a grade of 0.60, which clamps to `MAX_GRADE` and yields a factor of 5.396: the field would report a pace 5.4x faster than raw off a rise the gain path discards as noise. Even a single 1 m step is 0.20 grade and a factor of 2.50. This affects `grade_adjusted_pace` on all four rails (web, Dart, firmware, Garmin) identically, so it is not a Garmin defect and must not be fixed on one rail — it is a lockstep change to a registered constant set, plus a decision about whether the right instrument is a longer window or a rise threshold. Worst on a watch with no barometric altimeter, where `Activity.Info.altitude` is GPS altitude and the noise is metres, not tenths.
- [x] **The Garmin field picks its pace unit from `distanceUnits`, which may not be the setting the runner set for pace.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 964](../architecture/decisions.md)). Verified against the Connect IQ API docs rather than against an SDK: `System.DeviceSettings.paceUnits` exists, is `System.UnitsSystem` (`UNIT_METRIC` / `UNIT_STATUTE`) exactly as `distanceUnits` is, and is available since **API 1.0.0** against this app's `minApiLevel` of 3.1.0 — so every device in `manifest.xml` has it. One line, plus a sixth claim in `check_garmin_source.sh` and two cases in its suite, because the two members share a type: the wrong one compiles, runs, and is wrong only on a watch whose two preferences differ. Original filing below. `System.getDeviceSettings()` exposes distance and pace as separate unit preferences on Garmin devices, and a runner who logs distance in miles while reading pace in min/km is a real configuration. `GradeAdjustedPaceView.initialize` reads `distanceUnits`. Not changed in-round: the Connect IQ SDK is on no machine here, so which member exists and what it returns cannot be checked, and swapping to an API this lane cannot compile would trade a possible mislabel for a possible build break. Verify against the SDK docs the next time anyone has it installed; if `paceUnits` is the right member, the fix is one line and the value is read once at construction either way.
## Surfaced by the #789 coverage round 32 — infra + Lambda tier (2026-09-02)

Six defects this lane found were fixed in-round
([decisions §§ 949-953](../architecture/decisions.md)): the coach Lambda taking
the whole shared secrets file, `bin/key-rotate.sh` matching no rule in the
estate `.sops.yaml` on either env (so the compromise-response path was
unconditionally broken), five Lambda cores writing twenty bytes of the caller's
bearer token to CloudWatch, the osrm-proxy 405 with no `Allow`, a Function-URL
source guard that could not fail on a ninth Lambda left open, and a log-hygiene
reachability walk that stopped at the `$lib` import spelling. These are what the
lane found and did not take.

- [x] **The distribution-wide `404 -> /index.html at 200` rewrite destroys every Lambda origin's deliberate 404, and two Lambdas were written believing it does not.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1022](../architecture/decisions.md)) — and the proposed fix was the wrong one. The S3-never-404s premise **holds and was proved from this repo**: the site bucket policy is one statement granting `s3:GetObject` on `${bucket}/*` to `cloudfront.amazonaws.com` and nothing else (`s3:ListBucket` appears nowhere under `infra/` outside the two deploy-role policies), and the origin is `bucket_regional_domain_name` + OAC — the REST endpoint, not the `s3-website-` one that does 404. **But that is exactly why dropping the mapping is worse, not smaller**: the only responses the block ever sees are then the Lambdas' own, whose 404 bodies are `<p>This link isn't available.</p>` — unstyled, English-only, no navigation — and serving those would replace the SPA's designed localized not-found card (`share/run/[id]`'s `.notfound-card`, reached today ONLY because of this rewrite) on ten paths. `share-run/src/index.ts`'s own "the browser will fall back to the SPA's 404 surface" comment is true *because of* the mapping it describes as absent. The mapping now answers **404 with the shell body**: a crawler gets the status that de-indexes a URL (far more decisively than a `noindex` on a 200), a reader still lands on the app, and the bytes a viewer receives do not change at all. 403 stays at 200 and must. `scripts/check_infra_coverage.mjs` claim 4 fails any 4xx/5xx -> 2xx mapping, with the one SPA deep-link exemption declared and its reason recorded; a declared exemption nothing uses fails too. Original filing below. CloudFront models `custom_error_response` per DISTRIBUTION, not per behaviour, so the 404 mapping in `infra/modules/web-stack/main.tf` rewrites a share Lambda's not-found answer into the SPA shell at 200. Both `apps/web/lambda/share-run/src/index.ts` ("crawlers get a clean signal") and `apps/web/lambda/share-entity/src/index.ts` ("a clean crawler signal", "a 404 rather than guess") state the opposite in their own comments; main.tf's comment states the true behaviour and records it as MEASURED for the 403 case (issue #590, 2026-07-21). Consequence: every `/share/{run,route,recap,badge,event,profile,club,race,session,workout}/<id>` for a private, deleted or never-existing entity serves a crawler the generic SPA shell at 200 with **no `noindex`** — the tag exists only in a body that never ships — so those URLs are soft-404s Google is invited to index. The durable fix is to **drop the 404 mapping and keep the 403 one**: the site bucket policy grants `s3:GetObject` and nothing else (no `s3:ListBucket`), so S3 answers a missing key with 403 AccessDenied and never 404 — which is precisely why the 403 mapping exists and why the 404 one buys the SPA nothing. Not taken in-round because it is a production behaviour change this lane could neither `plan` nor verify (no AWS credentials, by design), and if the S3-never-404s premise is wrong it breaks every deep link at once. Verify it against the real distribution first (`curl -I https://threkir.com/share/run/<a-private-id>` should become a 404 carrying the Lambda's own body), then delete the `error_code = 404` block. The four share wrappers' new runtime suite already pins the `noindex` body, so the moment the mapping goes the assertion becomes a claim about what a crawler sees rather than about what a function returns.
- [x] **The three WAF rate-limit scope-downs match `uri_path` with `text_transformation = NONE`, while CloudFront's own behaviour matching normalises the path independently.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1023](../architecture/decisions.md)). `URL_DECODE` added at priority 1 on all three, **without a live measurement and deliberately so**: whether CloudFront decodes before behaviour matching is a fact about the edge and is NOT claimed here, but being wrong about it cannot cost anything, because on a search string containing no `%` decoding can only ADD matches — `%XX` becomes one byte and the string never lengthens, so a raw path whose first ten characters are already `/api/coach` still has them afterwards. It is a strict widening of a RATE LIMIT, never of an allow/deny; if CloudFront does not decode either, the cost is counting a request the edge was going to 404. `LOWERCASE` stays out and the guard now fails if anyone adds it. `scripts/check_infra_coverage.mjs` claim 5 also fails a rate-based rule with no readable scope-down — which would apply the counter to every static asset and turn a backstop into an outage. Original filing below. `infra/modules/web-stack/waf.tf` filters each rate-based rule to `STARTS_WITH "/api/coach"` / `"/api/routes/generate"` / `"/api/routes/osrm"` with a single `NONE` transformation. Two matchers, two normalisations: any encoded spelling CloudFront resolves to the behaviour but WAF does not resolve to the prefix reaches the Lambda with the per-IP cap not applied — and those three paths are the only ones on the distribution that cost money or engine CPU to serve. Standard hardening is a second `text_transformation` at priority 1 with `type = "URL_DECODE"` (adding `LOWERCASE` would be wrong here, because CloudFront path patterns are case-sensitive and `/API/coach` genuinely does not route to the Lambda). Not taken because it cannot be verified offline: whether CloudFront decodes before behaviour matching, and in what order WAF and a viewer-request function run, are both facts about the live edge rather than about this repo. Confirm with one `curl` against preview before changing prod.
- [ ] **The preview env's KMS key is not wired into the estate `.sops.yaml`, so nothing can encrypt a preview secrets file today.** Observed while verifying the `key-rotate.sh` fix against the real `../infra-secrets/.sops.yaml` (creation rules only — nothing decrypted, no ARN recorded): the `^running/prod\.sops\.yaml$` rule carries a resolved KMS ARN, and the `^running/preview\.sops\.yaml$` rule still carries the literal `KMS_RUNNING_PREVIEW_ARN_PLACEHOLDER` that `bin/sops-init.sh` writes and is supposed to replace. `sops` refuses to encrypt against a placeholder, so `bin/secret-set.sh preview <KEY>` cannot work and the preview Lambda env has whatever `terraform apply` last gave it. Not a repo defect — the fix is one operator action against the private estate repo (`aws sso login --profile running` then `bin/sops-init.sh preview`, which reads `terraform output kms_key_arn` from `infra/envs/preview` and seds the placeholder out) — but it was invisible until now because `key-rotate.sh`, the one script that reads that rule back, could not find any rule at all and reported the same sentence for a wired key and an unwired one. Filed so the state is written down somewhere in the open repo; the key material itself stays where it is.
- [x] **`generate-route` re-implements the body cap instead of importing the helper that exists to stop exactly that drift.** Closed round 33 ([decisions § 968](../architecture/decisions.md)) — and it was three of the four body-capping endpoints, not one: the coach's own two sub-paths also spelled their caps twice. The `400 invalid body encoding` branch is **not** dead code and was not deleted: unreachable through the declared string type, but a non-string body reaches it, and removing the catch turns a client-side malformation into a generic 503. Original text: `apps/web/src/lib/coach/body.ts` owns `decodeLambdaBody`, and its module comment records why: the coach's two wrappers once diverged on `bodyStr.length` (UTF-16 code units) versus decoded bytes, letting a multi-byte payload roughly three times the cap through. `apps/web/lambda/generate-route/src/index.ts` inlines its own `Buffer.from(...)` plus a `byteLength` check with a private `BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`. It is byte-correct today, so this is not a live defect — it is the same one-copy-per-wrapper shape, one Lambda over, with a source guard (`security_guards.test.ts`, "Coach endpoint enforces a 256 KB body cap on both wrappers") that names only the coach. Two smaller things ride along in the same file: `decodeLambdaBody`'s `400 invalid body encoding` branch is unreachable, because `Buffer.from(s, 'base64')` ignores invalid characters rather than throwing; and the coach wrapper's sub-path dispatch is `rawPath.includes('/route-describe')`, a substring test where a suffix test is meant. Neither is exploitable — every sub-path behind `/api/coach*` runs the same auth and paywall gates — but both read as stricter than they are.
## Surfaced by the #789 round 32 shared-packages lane (2026-09-02)

Five defects this lane found were fixed in-round with their pinning tests
([decisions §§ 954-958](../architecture/decisions.md)). What follows is what it
found and did not take.

- [x] **Every generated `double` field in `db_rows.dart` casts with `as num`, while the web twin's type for the same two columns is `number | string`.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 985](../architecture/decisions.md)). The premise is right and the string arrival is no longer hypothetical: measured over the local stack, `json_agg` — the shape PostgREST builds its body with — renders `'NaN'::numeric` as `"NaN"` and `'Infinity'::numeric` as `"Infinity"`, and `'NaN'::numeric >= 100` is **true**, so `global_segments_distance_m_check` admits precisely the value the cast cannot decode. The count was low: **69** generated `double` reads, not 50. `gen_dart_models.dart` now emits `_toDoubleOrNull` / `_toDouble` at the top of the file and every `double` column reads through them — a `num` or a parseable `String`, screened for finiteness, resolving to `null` for a nullable column and `double.nan` for a non-nullable one (never `0`, which is a plausible-looking lie where NaN is unmistakably no answer, and which is also exactly what web's `Number(...)` yields). Ints stay on `as num`: no integer Postgres type has a non-finite value and `to_json` never quotes one. Pinned by `packages/core_models/test/db_rows_numeric_test.dart`; reverting the generator and regenerating fails 6 of its 7 cases. `GlobalSegmentRow.fromJson` reads `distance_m` as `(json['distance_m'] as num).toDouble()`, and `catalogue_browse.dart`'s own doc block says web widens those fields "because PostgREST may hand a `numeric` column over as a JSON string" and asserts this side "has already coerced through `as num` at its own boundary". `as num` is a cast, not a coercion: if that string ever arrives, the cast throws a `TypeError` inside `fromJson` and the catalogue screen dies where web renders. The package already believes the wire can do this — `effort_rank.dart`'s `_usableRank` explicitly accepts `raw is String ? num.tryParse(raw)` — so the two boundaries in one package disagree about the same risk. 50 generated reads share the shape. Not taken in-round because `db_rows.dart` is generated and the fix belongs in `scripts/gen_dart_models.dart`, which no lane owns this round; the change is to emit a shared `_toDouble(Object?)` helper that accepts a `num` or a parseable `String` and to have every `double` column read through it. Verifying which columns PostgREST actually stringifies needs the local stack, which this lane did not own either.
- [x] **`ApiClient._uploadTrack` throws `JsonUnsupportedObjectError` on a non-finite waypoint, and only one of its five producers now screens for one.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 986](../architecture/decisions.md)). Confirmed in every particular, including that the throw is an `Error` and not an `Exception` (measured). The decision the filing declined to make: **drop the point, at the serializers rather than at the producers.** A non-finite coordinate is the absence of a location (§ 954), so dropping it removes nothing real, while refusing the upload leaves the runner with exactly what they have today — a run that never leaves the phone. `finiteWaypoints` in `core_models` is applied in `Run.toJson` (covering the local store's five encode sites and the backup archive at once), in the in-progress slice writer, and in `ApiClient._trackBlobJson`, so every one of the five producers and every future one is covered without a remember-to rule. The drop is counted and `debugPrint`ed at the upload site. A second instance was found in the same pass and taken: `Run.toJson` also failed to encode a non-finite `distanceMetres`, which would have taken the shared local index down with the run, and it now resolves to zero. **No terminal-error taxonomy was added**: the retry-forever loop is a symptom of a permanent failure existing, and removing the failure removes the loop — a category with no reachable member is a preemptive abstraction. Pinned by `packages/core_models/test/finite_track_test.dart` (7), two cases in `api_client_codecs_test.dart` and two in `local_run_store_test.dart`; making `finiteWaypoints` return its input unchanged fails all three suites. `jsonEncode(track.map(_waypointToJson).toList())` refuses a non-finite double, so a single such point makes the run unuploadable — and the local store's own `_encodeJson` fails the same way, so it is unsaveable too. The recorder's entry point is now guarded ([decisions § 956](../architecture/decisions.md)) and the four route importers are ([§ 954](../architecture/decisions.md)), but the tracks that reach `saveRun` from the Wear OS and watchOS bridges, from `strava_importer.dart`'s API path, from the backup-restore path, and from `resumeSession`'s caller-supplied seeded track are not. The failure is also the wrong SHAPE for the caller: it is an `Error`, it is indistinguishable from a transient upload failure, and the sync loop retries it forever. Filed rather than fixed because the honest answer is a decision this lane should not make alone — dropping the point silently alters the runner's track, and refusing the upload needs a terminal, classifiable error the sync drain can park rather than retry.
- [x] **`readAllPages` terminates on the first short page, so a deployment whose `db.max-rows` is below `kPostgrestPageSize` silently truncates.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 987](../architecture/decisions.md)). Confirmed by reading, and the fix took the first of the two shapes offered plus a half the filing did not name. The startup assertion was rejected because PostgREST does not tell a client its cap, so the assertion would have to infer it — which is what the loop now does, without a second mechanism to keep in step; **no backend change is needed and none was filed.** The half the filing missed: detecting the cap is not enough, the walk must also advance by the rows it RECEIVED rather than by the size it asked for, or a loop that noticed the truncation would skip the very rows the server withheld and turn it into a corruption. Stops on an empty page, or on a page both short of the ask and shorter than its predecessor. Cost is one extra round trip when the FIRST page is short (that page has no predecessor, and the two causes are indistinguishable without asking again); every other shape costs what it did. Measured over the local stack that a past-the-end range answers `200 []` — but `416` if the caller asks for an exact count, so that requirement is now written into the function's contract; none of the six callers asks. Pinned by four new cases in `paged_read_test.dart`, including a 1,400-row read against a server capping at 500; restoring the old rule fails three of them. The module's own doc says the server "caps at `db.max-rows` and answers with the truncated page and a 200 — no error, no flag", and then uses `page.length < pageSize` as the exhausted signal with `pageSize` fixed at 1000. If the cap is ever set below 1000, the first request comes back short and the loop reports a partial history as complete — the exact bug the function exists to remove, from the other side. `apps/backend/supabase/config.toml` sets no `max_rows`, so today this rests on the platform default matching the constant, with nothing anywhere asserting the two agree. The durable shape is for the paging loop to stop only on a page it asked for and did not fill AND that was shorter than the previous one, or for a startup assertion against the deployment's cap; either is a decision about the backend contract, which no lane owned this round.
- [x] **The mobile Routes screen tells the user Import "covers GPX / KML / KMZ / GeoJSON / TCX" and the picker offers two of them.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 988](../architecture/decisions.md)). Confirmed, and there were **four** disagreeing statements, not two: the screen comment said five formats, `routesEmptyBody` said **three** (GPX/KML/TCX — the filing read the comment as the copy), the picker took two, and `parity.md` marked GeoJSON, TCX and KML/KMZ all Android-`✓`. There were also **three** dispatches, not one — `routes_screen.dart`'s `_parseRouteFile` carried its own `ext == 'kml' ? 'kml' : 'gpx'` and never consulted `detectRouteFormat`, so the file-picker path could not have reached a new format even after the set widened. Widened for GeoJSON and TCX (both parsers already shipped and tested, just unreachable), picker allowlist now DERIVED from the format set plus a `json` -> `geojson` alias, the third dispatch deleted, sniff taught `<TrainingCenterDatabase` and a JSON opening, copy updated in all seven ARBs and pinned by a suite that reads them. **KMZ deliberately not added**: the blocker is not the parser but that the mobile pipeline is `String`-typed from `readAsString` through the `compute` request to the dispatch, and `readAsString` throws on a zip before any parser is reached — filed below. `parity.md`'s KML/KMZ row is split so KMZ reads `✗` on both mobile platforms. `routes_screen.dart`'s empty-state comment and `l10n.routesEmptyBody` say five formats; `FilePicker.pickFiles(allowedExtensions: ['gpx', 'kml'])` and `kSupportedRouteImportExtensions` allow two, and `routeFromImportedFile` dispatches to `fromKml`/`fromGpx` only, so a `.geojson` or `.tcx` handed in through the OS share sheet is parsed as GPX and fails. KMZ is worse: nothing in the Dart tree opens a zip, so it cannot work at all — this lane corrected the `gpx_parser` library docstring and pubspec description, which both claimed KMZ the package has never had an `archive` dependency to implement. Web accepts all five. Either widen the mobile picker and dispatch (GeoJSON and TCX are already parseable; KMZ needs an unzip step) or correct the copy; leaving it is a promise the app does not keep. `apps/mobile_android/` belongs to no lane this round, and the change is a twin edit plus an i18n key across seven ARBs.

## Surfaced by the #789 round 33 guard lane (2026-09-02)

- [x] **The `isTrackRenderable` 5 m span gate is still a bare literal on the web and Dart rails.** **CLOSED 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1028](../architecture/decisions.md)). Filed correctly in every particular. Named `MIN_RENDERABLE_SPAN_M` on web and `kMinRenderableSpanM` on the Dart twin (plus the iOS mirror), and registered as the three-rail `renderable-track span gate (m)` row. Each rail's test now makes two claims that fail to different mutations — the value flat, and two tracks bracketing the threshold by 1 cm THROUGH the constant, so a rail declaring it beside a literal that has drifted goes red; the flat assertion is what says which number, because the registry compares the rails against each other and moving all three together would satisfy it. The firmware's own test comment, which said the other two rails could not be registered, was corrected in the same change. Original filing follows. The wrist half is closed: `apps/custom_watch/core/src/track_projection.rs` now declares `MIN_RENDERABLE_SPAN_M` and compares against it, with a test that fails both when the value moves and when the comparison stops reading the constant. Web's `apps/web/src/lib/routes/track_projection.ts` still ends `isTrackRenderable` on `> 5`, and the Dart twin inside `apps/mobile_android/lib/widgets/track_preview.dart` on `> 5` at line 488. `scripts/check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs` reads a rail by the NAME of its constant (`tsConst` / `dartConst`), so until both are named the three cannot be registered as a `CONSTANT_ROWS` row and the number is held together by nothing — the same shape the live-pace ceiling was in before this round. Closing it is one named constant on each of the two rails (`MIN_RENDERABLE_SPAN_M` / `kMinRenderableSpanM`, to match the existing `ELEVATION_GAIN_MIN_DELTA_M` / `kElevationGainMinDeltaM` pair) plus a three-rail row. Not taken here because `apps/web/` and `apps/mobile_android/` belong to other lanes this round.
- [x] **`main` was red at this round's base commit, on `Test Flutter packages`.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 991](../architecture/decisions.md)) — the guard lane recorded it and could not own it; the mobile lane root-caused it in the same round. The failure was `sync_service_test.dart` racing its own `tearDown` into `errno 39`, and the cause sat one layer below the test: `didChangeAppLifecycleState` and `start()` are `void` and discarded `_trySync`'s future, so nothing could observe a cycle finishing and the test's `saveBatchCallCount` assertion was satisfied before `markManySynced` had written. `SyncService` now holds the in-flight cycle. Original filing follows. Run 33690185523 against `bb87b5ab39d20331840781cea1f206b60d8abce5` (PR #850, 2026-09-02 22:24Z) failed that job and therefore the `CI gate`; the two runs before it were green. Recorded rather than investigated: this lane owns `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `apps/watch_garmin/` and `apps/custom_watch/`, none of which that job reads, and chasing a Flutter failure from a guard lane would have meant editing another lane's files mid-round. Whoever integrates round 33 should confirm it is not inherited into the merge.

## Surfaced by the #789 round 33 Lambda lane (2026-09-02)

Five filings closed in-round with their pinning tests ([decisions §§ 967-971](../architecture/decisions.md)); four of the five were wrong before they were anything else, and the corrections are recorded above and in the ADRs. What follows is what this lane found and did not take.

- [x] **Eight guard tests carry their own copy of a comment stripper, and the correct order is now enforced but not single-sourced.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1000](../architecture/decisions.md)). Thirteen spellings across twelve files, not eight: the filing's walker was the ordering guard's own, which reached `src/lib/**/*.test.ts` only, and four more lived under `tests-e2e/` — three of them in the wrong order, none of them hiding anything today (measured: byte-identical output either way over every file those three scan). Single-sourced into `src/lib/core/strip_comments.ts`, a one-pass scanner rather than another chain of `.replace` calls, because the string-literal case the filing names cannot be closed by a substitution — nor can the regex-literal case underneath it, which no copy handled either. Strings and regex literals are emitted verbatim so a misread can only leave a comment standing, never delete code. The ordering guard is replaced by a register of every file still allowed to spell a block strip, with its count and reason, staleness-checked in both directions. One copy remains by design: `src/lib/integrations/strava_zip_strictness.test.ts` was another lane's this round, and is a register entry naming that reason. Original filing below. [§ 971](../architecture/decisions.md) fixed the ordering in all six that strip both comment forms, and `security_guards.test.ts` now fails a PR that puts the block strip first — so the class cannot regress. What it does not do is remove the duplication: `site_url.test.ts`, `lambda_site_origin.test.ts`, `coach_lambda_handler.test.ts`, `security_guards.test.ts`, `lambda_log_hygiene.test.ts` and `paged_read_guards.test.ts` each spell the same four-line `code()` helper, and `cloud_export_transport.test.ts` + `strava_zip_strictness.test.ts` spell a two-`replace` variant of it. Eight copies of one rule is the same shape [§ 968](../architecture/decisions.md) and [§ 970](../architecture/decisions.md) are about, one layer up. The durable fix is a single exported `stripComments` the guards import; not taken in-round because it means editing test files across four lanes' territory in a round where five agents share one checkout, and because the ordering guard already makes a wrong copy fail loudly. Whoever takes it should also handle the one case none of the eight handles: a `/*` inside a STRING literal, which opens a phantom block exactly as the `//` case did.
- [x] **The two CSS comment scanners cannot see a `//` and do not need to, but nothing records that.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1001](../architecture/decisions.md)). A sentence in each header, and the skip is now DECLARED rather than detected: § 1000's register lists each CSS scanner with the number of block-comment strips it may spell and why, and fails when that count moves — so a reader who "fixes" one to match the JS guards fails the guard instead of quietly blanking a protocol-relative `url()`. `security_guards.test.ts` is in the register too, for the same reason: both its `<style>`-block scans are CSS. Original filing below. `contrast_guard.test.ts` and `rtl_css_guards.test.ts` strip `/* … */` alone and are correct — `//` is not a comment in CSS — but they sit beside six guards where stripping block comments alone was the defect, and the new ordering guard deliberately skips them by detecting that they strip only one form. A reader who "fixes" them to match the others would start blanking real CSS containing `//` (a protocol-relative URL, a `content:` string). One sentence in each file's header would close it; not taken because both files are outside this lane's scope.
- [x] **Consider a method gate on the five share Lambdas, or accept the OPTIONS render.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1005](../architecture/decisions.md)). The `curl` was not needed: a CORS preflight only succeeds against a response carrying `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, and NEITHER the five handlers NOR `aws_cloudfront_response_headers_policy.security` emits any `access-control-*` header — checked both — so a browser preflight against these paths already fails and no crawler sends one. Two things the filing did not have: `cached_methods` is `["GET", "HEAD"]`, so OPTIONS is the one allowed method the edge cache cannot absorb (a GET storm costs one render per five-minute window, an OPTIONS storm one render per request), and the in-repo clients were swept for a preflight-triggering fetch to `/share/*` or `/og/*` — there are none. One shared `shareMethodRefusal` rather than five copies, fail-closed on an absent method, `Allow: GET, HEAD`, `no-store`. Driven for real against all five handlers on OPTIONS / POST / DELETE / no-method, with HEAD pinned as still rendering. Original filing below. [§ 972](../architecture/decisions.md) added the guard that keeps `allowed_methods` narrow, which is what makes the missing gate safe. It leaves one thing measured and unaddressed: `OPTIONS` IS in `allowed_methods` and IS forwarded to the origin, and an `OPTIONS /og/run/<id>.png` runs a full ~50 ms `resvg` render and answers `200 image/png` — on paths the WAF rate-limit rules do not scope. Adding the gate turns that into a 405, which is almost certainly right (nothing should preflight a crawler-facing image URL) but could not be verified from this lane against the live distribution. Decide it with one `curl -X OPTIONS` against preview before changing five handlers.
- [x] **`lambda_site_origin.test.ts` is now named for a scope it no longer has.** **CLOSED 2026-09-02** ([decisions § 1002](../architecture/decisions.md)). Verified: the file drives `buildShareRunMeta` / `renderShareRunHeadTags` / `buildShareEventHead` / `renderShareEventHeadTags` and reads no Lambda source at all. `git mv` to `share_head_origin.test.ts`, header rewritten to say why the `lambda_` prefix was once right, inventory line added. Original filing below. Its `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` caller register moved to `core/site_url.test.ts` in [§ 970](../architecture/decisions.md), because that file already walked `src` and `lambda` together for the sibling scan. What remains under the `lambda_` name is two behavioural tests about what the share head builders emit under a misconfigured env — true of the Lambdas but stated through the shared `$lib/share` builders, so the name over-narrows what it covers exactly as the body-cap guard's name did in [§ 968](../architecture/decisions.md). Renaming it to `share_head_origin.test.ts` is a `git mv` plus a line in `docs/testing/test_inventory.md`; not taken in-round to keep the diff on that inventory file small while four other lanes are appending to it.

Two consequences of [decisions § 981](../architecture/decisions.md) that this
lane's paths could not reach, plus one guard shape worth copying.

Adapter deleted; the page calls `Math.round(computeElevationGain(run.track))`. Measured before deciding: BOTH of the adapter's guards were dead — the caller already tests `run?.track`, and `computeElevationGain` returns 0 for an empty track and for a single point — so the whole adapter was `Math.round`. Original filing below. § 981 made `runs/run_stats.ts`'s `elevationGainMetres` delegate to `routes/route_simplify.ts`'s `computeElevationGain` so the app has one elevation rule rather than two. It was left as an adapter only because its single call site — `apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte:801`, `run?.track ? elevationGainMetres(run.track) : 0` — is outside the paths this lane owned. The tidy end state is the one mobile already has: delete the adapter, and have the page call `Math.round(computeElevationGain(run.track))` the way `run_detail_screen.dart` calls the Dart twin. Two files (`run_stats.ts` + the page) plus moving the four `elevationGainMetres` cases in `run_stats.test.ts` onto whatever survives; the "one rule" case added by § 981 is the one that must not be lost, since it is the only thing pinning that the run stat and the route summary answer identically.

It no longer does: web has one rule now, and it is the gated one. The watch is a one-way port outside the enforced lockstep so nothing fails today, but a device that renders a run's vert from `run_stats` and a loaded course's from `route_simplify` will disagree with itself on the same terrain, which is exactly what § 981 measured (143 m of climb on a flat half-hour).
