### Surfaced by the #789 round 36 mobile lane (2026-09-03)

Three boxes taken, all three ticked in place above. One of the three filings
described shipped behaviour and was itself the defect; a second's census of the
work remaining had drifted in three of its four numbers. What follows is what
this lane found and could not take.

- [x] **`debugWritesSettled()` deadlocks rather than failing when its zone precondition is unmet, and nothing says so at the call site.** [decisions § 1072](../architecture/decisions.md) measured the rule: the probe is only awaitable when the write it waits on was queued from inside `tester.runAsync`, because `serialiseStoreWrite` links its chain with `.then` and a fake-zone continuation is a microtask only `pump` drains. The failure mode is the worst shape available — a test that hangs to the runner's timeout with no message, which on CI reads as an infrastructure flake rather than as a misuse. The doc comment on `OfflineSyncStore.debugWritesSettled` names the race it closes but not the precondition. Two options, neither taken here because the fix belongs beside the helper rather than beside a caller: state the precondition in the doc comment (cheap, and enough for a reader who is already looking), or make the probe *detect* it — the chain could record the zone each link was queued from and the probe could throw a named error naming the offending call site. The second is the durable one; it wants a look at whether `Zone.current` is a usable discriminator inside `runAsync` before anyone commits to it. **Closed 2026-09-03** — [§ 1093](../architecture/decisions.md). `Zone.current` was measured first and is not a discriminator: across five configurations run in isolated processes, the queueing and awaiting zones are non-identical in all four cases where the comparison is defined, two of which settle and two of which hang — and because every `tester.runAsync` forks a fresh zone, an identity check would have fired on `nutrition_screen_test`, the file that proves the helper works. A drainability probe fails too. So the wait is bounded on `Zone.root` and completes with a `StateError` naming the precondition, the `pumpUntil` remedy and the call site, and all three wrappers state the precondition in their doc comments. The measurement also corrected the rule twice: an intervening `pump` does not rescue a fake-zone write, and a fake-zone await hangs as readily as a `runAsync` one.
- [x] **26 mobile test files pair a temp directory with widget taps and no `pumpUntil` at all, and the sweep is now actionable.** The earlier survey filed this as a population with no stated remedy, which is why nobody has worked it. § 1072 supplies the missing half: after a fake-zone tap, wait on an **observable outcome** with `pumpUntil`; `debugWritesSettled` is for a **real-zone** write, and reaching for it otherwise deadlocks. With that rule the 26 are triage rather than research. Two of them (`gym_exercise_screen_test.dart`, `route_builder_screen_test.dart`) delete the temp dir from `addTearDown`, which is the shape that races a write in flight; the rest use `try/finally` or `tearDown`, which race it just as readily. Not taken here because it is a sweep, not a fix, and this lane's three items already carried one. **Swept and closed 2026-09-03 — nothing needed converting** ([§ 1097](../architecture/decisions.md)). Re-counted first: naively 27 at `076b624c8` over 89 temp-dir files, and **25** once comment text is excluded — two "members" match only on a comment saying why the file does NOT use `pumpAndSettle`, the same defect § 1072 found in the `pumpEventQueue` count. Both files named as the worst shape are non-members (`gym_exercise_screen_test.dart` writes inside `runAsync` and its one tap navigates; `route_builder_screen_test.dart` saves in real-zone `test()` bodies and its widget taps drive a dialog that pops a result). The discriminator also misses the other way: the two real members were fixed by § 1012 and still count, because their correct lever is `debugInProgressSettled`, not `pumpUntil`. All 25 scanned for a tap followed by a store assertion — zero — plus the four highest-risk hand-read.
- [x] **Web's `provider_probe.ts` has no registered Dart twin, and the probe rule now lives on both platforms unregistered.** [decisions § 1073](../architecture/decisions.md) moved mobile onto web's `probeSaysConfigured` rule — configured iff the invoke did not throw — but stated it natively inside `RaceService.isProviderConfigured` rather than as a `provider_probe.dart`. Two reasons, and only the first is about taste: a one-call-site helper wrapping a `try`/`catch` is a preemptive abstraction, and — decisively — a Dart twin would be a new **parity pair**, which needs rows in BOTH the root `CLAUDE.md` table and `.claude/agents/shared-library-syncer.md`, neither of which the mobile lane owns. A pair named by one registry is a pair whose divergence nothing detects ([§ 641](../architecture/decisions.md)), so half-registering it would be worse than not registering it. The rule is now duplicated across platforms with nothing comparing the two, which is exactly the shape § 641 and [§ 852](../architecture/decisions.md) were both about. Do it in a change that owns the root `CLAUDE.md`: either register the pair, or record in both modules' headers that the rule is deliberately single-sourced per platform and why. Cheap either way; the cost of leaving it is that the next divergence is invisible. **Closed 2026-09-03 — not registered** ([§ 1095](../architecture/decisions.md)). The two halves have no shared signature: `@supabase/functions-js` RETURNS `{data, error}` while Dart's `functions_client` THROWS, so a Dart twin would take an error value no Dart caller holds and a pair's syncer would have no computation to compare. What the pair would have bought is bought directly instead — `race_providers_test.dart` now reads `provider_probe.ts` and fails if it stops exporting `probeSaysConfigured`, stops being the nullish check, or grades a status again. `race_service.dart`'s header records the decision; **the reciprocal note in `provider_probe.ts`'s header is still owed** — the mobile lane cannot edit `apps/web/`.
- [x] **The parked-push state is mobile-only, and deliberately owes web nothing — worth saying so before someone files it as a § 24 inversion.** [§ 1070](../architecture/decisions.md)'s `blocked_runs.json`, `RunPushOutcome` and the run-detail card exist because the phone has a local queue that retries; the web app is always online and has no unsynced-run concept at all (`parity.md`'s "Bulk sync button" row already records that). `RunPushOutcome` lives in `core_models` rather than in `api_client` so the store can read it without a client dependency, not because a second platform is expected to consume it. If web ever grows an offline queue this is the design to mirror; until then a missing web surface here is correct. **Confirmed and closed 2026-09-03** — [§ 1096](../architecture/decisions.md). Re-verified against the code, not the entry: `blocked_runs.json` + `RunPushOutcome` + the run-detail parked card are all live on mobile, `apps/web/src/lib` contains no reference to an unsynced queue or a blocked run at all, and `local_run_store.dart` imports `core_models` and `flutter/foundation` only — which is the layering reason the outcome type sits there. Recorded as a `parity.md` row of its own beside the bulk-sync row, marked N/A for web with the reason, so the next reader meets it in the matrix rather than in an ADR.
### Surfaced by the #789 round 36 backend / SQL lane (2026-09-03)

- [x] **`TestRedisHub_SubscribeWithHistoryReplaysThenStreams` flaked once on CI, and the obvious explanation is measurably wrong.** It failed on PR #854 (run 33798704651) with `timed out waiting for the live ping` after 1 s, in a tree that PR does not touch, having passed the previous four runs. The natural diagnosis is that `rdb.Subscribe` returns before Redis has registered the subscription, so the `Publish` immediately after `SubscribeWithHistory` is dropped by a server with no subscriber yet — which would also undermine the SUBSCRIBE-to-LRANGE window reasoning the surrounding comment rests on, and would make a spectator miss their first ping. **Measured, and it does not happen**: a probe that builds a fresh miniredis, subscribes, takes `Channel()` and publishes immediately, 300 times under `-race`, lost **0 of 300**. `Channel()` establishes the subscription before it returns. So that is ruled out and the hypothesis should not be re-derived. What remains unexplained is a plain 1-second deadline missed under `-race` on a 2-core shared runner while `go test -race ./...` runs every package at once — goroutine starvation rather than a lost message. It could not be reproduced here: 40 runs of the single test and 6 runs of the whole `livehub` package under `-race` all passed. **Raising the deadline is not the fix and must not be the fix** — if a message can be lost, a longer wait never finds it; if it is starvation, a longer wait hides how slow the path became. Closing it needs an instrumented reproduction that records whether the forwarder goroutine ever received the message, which distinguishes the two in one run. Owner tree: `apps/job_worker/internal/livehub/`. **Closed 2026-09-03 — and the filing's rule-out was itself wrong** ([§ 1113](../architecture/decisions.md)). The message CAN be lost. The 0-of-300 probe ran on an idle box and called `Channel()` on its own goroutine where `startForwarder` calls it inside one; re-probed under the condition the flake occurred in (two cores saturated, `-race`), the same round lost **8 of 400**, every loss with `PUBLISH` reporting **zero receivers** — the server saying it had no subscriber at that instant. `Client.Subscribe` calls `pubsub.Subscribe`, DISCARDS its error, and that writes the SUBSCRIBE and releases the connection without reading a reply; go-redis's own `ExamplePubSub` does a `Receive` for exactly this reason. Both subscribe paths now block for the `*Subscription` confirmation: **0 of 400** on the identical load. The deadline was not raised. The test now keeps the receiver count and, on a missed deadline, waits a grace window before failing so it says whether the ping was lost or merely late; the regression pin is 25 rounds down both paths asserting one receiver each, which fails within a few rounds on the unfixed code under load and passes 20 consecutive `-race` runs on the fixed one. `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` green across all 14 packages.

Four items closed in-round ([decisions §§ 1076-1080](../architecture/decisions.md)),
three of them on filings that were wrong about their own premise. What follows is
what the lane found and could not take, plus the one thing the closed items
sequenced rather than finished.

- [x] **The frozen 1,488-pair case-fold table is now affordable and is still not built.** This is the surviving half of the entry above. [§ 830](../architecture/decisions.md) closed the *collation* dependence; the *runtime-version* one is untouched and measured — after the two named folds the three rails still disagree at **465** code points between web and mobile, **410** between mobile and the server, **55** between web and the server (Cherokee, Vithkuqi, Garay, Medefaidrin, Latin Extended-D/E, supplementary planes). The blocker was cost: `translate()` over the table is 60 µs a call against 0.34 µs for `lower()`, and five RPCs re-derived the key once per `gym_sets` row. [§ 1076](../architecture/decisions.md) removed that — the fold is now paid once per WRITE, so the table's cost is bounded by how often a lifter logs a set. What remains is the table itself, on three rails: `EXERCISE_*` in `gym_prs.ts`, `gym_prs.dart`, and `normalise_exercise_name`. Two notes for whoever takes it. The SQL rail is cheap to WRITE — `create or replace function` plus the keyset backfill `20270706000002` establishes, no rewrite, because the key is trigger-maintained and not generated — **but it cannot ship on its own, measured 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1102](../architecture/decisions.md)). Three VALIDATED CHECKs name the function (`gym_sets_exercise_key_canonical`, `gym_routine_exercises_exercise_key_canonical`, `exercises_name_key_canonical`), two of them over client-stamped columns, so the function is the acceptance predicate the other two rails write against. Demonstrated in a rolled-back transaction: replace the function so it folds one extra code point, and a row stored under the old fold survives (Postgres re-checks nothing) but `update t set name = name` — a no-op self-update — raises 23514, a fresh insert of the same pair is refused, and `validate constraint` fails. Blast radius measured: Postgres's ICU lowercase map is non-identity at 1,433 code points, a current single-char table (Unicode 16.0) at 1,459, and they disagree at 28 — 27 the newer table lowercases and ICU does not (U+1C89, U+A7CB/CC/DA/DC, the Garay block U+10D50-52 and 19 more), one the other way (U+0130, already folded by name since § 830), and **zero** mapping to different values. So the SQL-only edit moves the fold at exactly the newest-block code points the table exists to protect, and makes every stored key containing one of them un-updatable. The three rails move together or not at all. The CLIENT rails are the expensive ones and they are where the divergence lives: mobile's `exercise_key` writes to `gym_routine_exercises` and `exercises` are still client-stamped under a validated CHECK, which is the path § 830 measured a 23514 on. An ASCII-only fold is **not** the cheap alternative: 397 code points between U+00C0 and U+052F fold identically on all three rails today and it would stop folding every one, splitting "Überzüge" from "überzüge". Owner trees: `apps/web/src/lib/gym/`, `apps/mobile_android/lib/`, `scripts/check_shared_constants.mjs` — no single lane owned all three this round. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1175](../architecture/decisions.md) + [§ 1176](../architecture/decisions.md) + [§ 1177](../architecture/decisions.md) + [§ 1178](../architecture/decisions.md)).** All three rails moved in one change: the frozen Unicode 17.0 SIMPLE-lowercase table is generated by `scripts/gen_exercise_fold_table.mjs` into `apps/web/src/lib/gym/exercise_fold_table.ts` + `apps/mobile_android/lib/exercise_fold_table.dart` and into the new `public.exercise_fold_case` (migration `20270709000010`), and no rail reaches for its runtime's `toLowerCase()` / `lower()` any more. **Residual disagreement is zero**: every assignable code point through each rail's whole shipped pipeline, chunk-hashed, gives md5 `76a152d0e2a86b0b39a311597b42633b` on all three -- 465 / 410 / 55 becomes 0 / 0 / 0. **Two of this entry's numbers were wrong.** The ICU-vs-frozen-table delta is not 28 (27 one way, 1 the other): measured on this box it is **55 one way and 0 the other**, because the 28 was taken against Unicode **16.0** and the "1 the other way" was U+0130, a differing VALUE rather than a fold ICU has and the table lacks. Everything else re-measured true -- 465 / 410 / 55, the 1,488 pairs, 60.2 us against 0.35 us. A third thing the entry could not have known: **web does not move at all**, because the frozen table IS web's own answer -- over 8,896,512 strings (every code point in eight contexts) the old and new web pipelines differ on zero, so the whole move is bringing mobile and the server onto what web already said. Blast radius on real rows: 0 of 23 `gym_sets`, 0 of 4 `gym_routine_exercises`, 0 of 43 `exercises` re-key. Simple rather than FULL mapping because a per-code-point table can carry neither a context (Final_Sigma, still folded by name) nor a 1:many expansion (U+0130, now a table entry -- its hand-written pre-fold is deleted from all three rails); every entry being 1:1 is what lets the SQL rail be a `translate()`. The `collate "und-x-icu"` pin goes with the `lower()` it pinned, so the derivation is now collation-FREE rather than collation-pinned and the `immutable` marking is true in fact. `scripts/check_shared_constants.mjs` compares the three tables, the version stamps and the SQL ASCII fast path against the table's own ASCII half; there is deliberately no re-render guard ([§ 1176](../architecture/decisions.md)) because the table is frozen rather than tracking.
- [x] **`auth-email` has no positive-path test, and it is not blocked on a credential.** (Closed 2026-09-03 — [decisions § 1100](../architecture/decisions.md).) The filing was right on every point including the SMTP one. `ci.yml`'s boot step now writes `SMTP_HOST=host.docker.internal` / `SMTP_PORT=54325` / `SMTP_FROM` beside the hook secret — `127.0.0.1` is the functions CONTAINER's own loopback, and the CLI starts that container with `--add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway`, which is why the committed `supabase/functions/.env` already uses that pair (the network alias `inbucket:1025` resolves from there too and would have worked equally). The case signs a signup payload, POSTs, and reads the delivered mail out of Mailpit. Two assertions, both checked for discriminating power against the live host: the subject must be the FRENCH catalogue entry (the same payload with no locale renders `Confirm your email address`, with `de-DE` renders `Bestätige deine E-Mail-Adresse`), and the body must carry this run's unique `token_hash`. The payload carries no `user.id`, so the handler skips its `user_settings` read and the case needs no service-role key. Mail is found by searching on the recipient, never by clearing the catcher. 25/25 handler-envelope cases pass against a host booted the way CI boots it; negative control with a wrong secret fails at the 200 assertion with `401 bad_signature`. [§ 1079](../architecture/decisions.md) found the "positive-path Edge Function tests" filing wrong and this is the honest residue. The Standard Webhooks secret is ours (`ci.yml` already writes `SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET` into `.env.local`) and Mailpit is already in the local stack, so a correctly-signed request would deliver and be assertable against the Mailpit API — the same shape the three `stripe-events-webhook` side-effect cases already use. What blocks it is that the function reads `SMTP_HOST` / `SMTP_PORT` / `SMTP_FROM`, none of which is in `.env.local`, and adding them means editing `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That file was outside this lane. The one real subtlety: the function runs inside the edge-runtime container, so the host must be reachable from there (`host.docker.internal` or the Mailpit container name), not `127.0.0.1`. Owner tree: `.github/`.
- [x] **`refresh-tokens` has no positive-path test, and this one genuinely needs a mocked upstream.** (Closed 2026-09-03 — [decisions § 1101](../architecture/decisions.md).) **The filing is wrong on both halves.** The seam it names is a `globalThis.fetch` stub, not an injectable parameter, and `refresh-tokens/lib.test.ts` has been using it since PR #438: "refresh-tokens routes through the CAS helper with the read refresh token" drives the success branch through a stubbed Strava token response and asserts `refreshed === 1` plus the compare-and-swap arguments, and `sweep_invariants.test.ts` adds "each integration is refreshed with its OWN token, and the count is the successes" — 16 unit tests, all passing. Building an injection parameter would have been a second seam for a solved problem. What was genuinely missing sits one layer up: all three `refresh-tokens` cases in `handler_envelope.test.ts` are 403s, so a handler that refused everything passed all three and the gate OPENING had no coverage anywhere. Added, and it needs no upstream either — the fixture is an integration inside the sweep's one-hour window (so the select is not empty, which is what would make the 200 vacuous) holding no vault secret, so `get_integration_tokens` yields nothing and the loop `continue`s before `refreshStravaToken`; that the upstream was not contacted is then observed rather than assumed, because a real call with an unusable grant would 4xx and stamp `disconnected_at`, which the test reads back. Its success branch POSTs to strava.com's OAuth token endpoint with a real client secret and a real refresh token, so no test-chosen secret reaches it — this is the narrow case the closed filing described in general terms and is true only here. The durable shape is an injectable token-exchange fetch (the `_shared/strava_upstream.test.ts` seam already exists for the import path) rather than a live credential in CI. Owner tree: `apps/backend/supabase/functions/refresh-tokens/` — not taken this round because the lane's own items were larger, not because it is blocked.
- [x] **`donations_status_lock_test.sql` fails on this workstation and passes on CI, and the divergence is now costing a lane a diagnosis every round.** (Closed 2026-09-03 — [decisions § 1098](../architecture/decisions.md), migration `20270707000001`.) The filing's shape was right and its size was not: enumerating "the routines the default currently covers" is the work, and the answer is **one**. Measured against the local image, where `proacl` is exactly `{postgres}` plus what a migration stated: the 7 RPCs the Edge Functions call as service_role and the 5 the Go worker calls already carry an explicit `service_role` entry; all 95 RPC names the web / Lambda / mobile / `api_client` trees call already carry an explicit `authenticated` entry and none has a NULL `proacl`; every base table already grants service_role the four DML verbs by name (`20270702000002`); and the 74 functions still on a NULL `proacl` are trigger bodies whose every out-of-migration reference is a comment, not a call. So the migration grants `fundraiser_totals(uuid)` to `service_role` and nothing else — `fundraiser_feed` is deliberately refused, having no service_role caller. `anon_execute_registry_test.sql` gains the positive half of its registry (the role holds EXECUTE, and holds it through an entry naming that role rather than through PUBLIC or a NULL `proacl`), with its CI-vacuity limit stated. Before: `Files=286, Tests=2601`, `donations_status_lock_test` bad plan (19 planned, 0 ran). After: `Files=286, Tests=2622`, all pass. It dies at its first `fundraiser_totals` call with `permission denied for function`, as `service_role`. Measured on the local stack: `fundraiser_totals`' ACL is `{postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X}` — no `service_role` — and `20270630000001` issues no explicit grant for it, relying on Supabase's `alter default privileges`. The workstation CLI is 2.109.1 and CI pins 2.84.2, and the two images disagree about which roles that default covers. Nothing in the repo is wrong today, but the durable fix is the house form § 790 already established for `normalise_exercise_name`: grant EXECUTE **by name** to every role that must call the function, rather than inheriting whatever the image's default privileges happen to be. That is a migration re-emitting the grants for the routines the default currently covers, and deciding the list per routine is the work. Owner tree: `apps/backend/supabase/migrations/` — filed rather than taken because the list needs a deliberate per-routine judgement, not a sweep.
## Surfaced by the #789 round 36 Wear OS / infra lane (2026-09-03)

Four items closed ([decisions §§ 1082-1085](../architecture/decisions.md)), one
verification item re-run and left open for the reason it was already open (no
lane holds AWS credentials, so nothing is `plan`ned). No filing in this lane's
set turned out to be wrong. What follows is what the lane found and could not,
or deliberately did not, take.

- [x] **A corrupt run queue is invisible on the pre-run screen, and the count that would show it is frozen.** **CLOSED 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1104](../architecture/decisions.md)). Both calls made deliberately. **(a) Retry, not `retry`-vs-`catch` by taste**: catching is not a judgement about corruption, it is a judgement that the first failure is the last one, and a read is one file open — so `store.queue` is `retryWhen`-ed, unbounded, with `queueReadRetryDelayMs` doubling 1 s → 60 s. Deliberately NOT `DrainBackoff`'s 60 s → 30 min curve: that throttles a network round trip, this throttles a local open whose failure takes the recovery affordance off screen. The shift is clamped because `1_000L shl 64` is `1_000L shl 0` on the JVM and an unclamped exponent silently resets the backoff to its base. **(b) The counted chip's own slot becomes a retry chip**, claiming no figure — "Sync ?" and a persistent error line both rejected for the reasons filed, and what was missing was the affordance rather than a sentence. Not gated on `online` (the read is local and the network is not a party to it), still gated on `authed` (`drainQueue` returns from `awaitAuth()` before reading anything), and the warning colour is not the only signal — the label differs and the content description carries the whole sentence. `queueUnreadable` is a second field rather than a nullable count so "never read yet" cannot flash the chip on every cold start, and BOTH readers of the file write it so the drain and the chip cannot disagree. 8 new Wear tests (74 classes / 725 at that commit, from 717). Original filing below. [§ 1082](../architecture/decisions.md) makes the drain report an unreadable queue as `syncError`, which renders on `PostRunScreen` only — the screen the runner is on immediately after the run that just entered the queue, which is where it matters most. It does NOT render on `PreRunScreen`, whose "Sync N runs" chip is gated on `queuedCount > 0`, and `queuedCount` comes from `observeQueue`'s collection of `store.queue` — a flow whose [§ 1055](../architecture/decisions.md) `.catch` TERMINATES it. So after one failed read the count is frozen at its last value for the life of the process (0 on a cold start), the chip never appears, and a runner who reboots into a corrupt queue is shown nothing at all. Two decisions sit underneath and neither is the drain's: whether the queue stream should be `retry`ed rather than caught (a corrupt DataStore file will fail again, but the failure could also be transient I/O), and what a pre-run surface should say on a 1.4-inch screen when the count itself is unknown — "Sync ?" is worse than silence, a persistent error line competes with the battery and recovery notices already anchored there. Entirely inside `apps/watch_wear/`. Not taken because it is a UI/state design decision, not the saved-data one the closed filing asked for, and picking it by default is the mistake that filing warned about.
- [x] **`RecordingRepository.Metrics.avgBpm` carries two different claims at two different times.** **CLOSED 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1105](../architecture/decisions.md)). `Metrics` carries `finishedHr: HeartRateClaim?` — the pair § 1083 already returns — written once by whoever makes the `Finished` transition and null everywhere else; null claims no heart rate rather than falling back. **The filing's premise was wrong in the direction that made the fix better**: the rolling mean is not "the live figure the running screen renders". `RunningScreen` takes the instantaneous `bpm`, the active-run tile carries no heart rate at all, and the grader reads the raw `bpmSum`/`bpmCount` off the service rather than off this state — so the live write had NO reader between the sample that produced it and the stop that overwrote it, and its only effect was the hazard. It is therefore deleted, not renamed. That hazard was real: `update` is a CAS loop because five writers race on it and cancellation cannot interrupt a non-suspending call in flight, so the collect's transform could land after the stop's and restore an ungraded mean over an average the grader had suppressed. **On the source guard**: split by whether a type can express it. "Both save paths grade through `heartRateClaim`" stays a source guard — that two named call sites call one function is not a Kotlin type. The ordering assertion is DELETED rather than converted, because its premise goes with the second writer. Replacing it: one real test that applies the collect's transform after the stop's on the actual repository and asserts the suppressed claim survives, plus a scan widened from the two save bodies to the whole recorder — the collect was dividing the pair in a body the old guard deliberately excluded. Original filing below. During a run it is the live rolling mean the running screen renders; at `Finished` it is the graded claim [§ 1083](../architecture/decisions.md) produced, because `stopRecording` overwrites it in the same `update`. `RunViewModel.handleFinishedRun` reads the field and cannot tell which it got — it is correct only because the overwrite happens first, and `HeartRateCoverageTest` pins that ordering with a source guard rather than a type. The durable shape is a separate field (or a `FinishedHeartRate` on the `Finished` transition) so the ungraded live figure is not reachable from the save path at all. Small, `apps/watch_wear/` only, and deliberately not bundled into the change that introduced the grading.
- [x] **Nothing reads `hr_coverage`, so a suppressed `avg_bpm` is indistinguishable from a run with no heart rate at all.** [§ 1083](../architecture/decisions.md) writes the key and states that its most useful reading is when the average is ABSENT — but every reader of `avg_bpm` (`apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte`, `apps/mobile_android/lib/screens/run_detail_screen.dart`, the export CSV) renders nothing when it is missing, which is the same thing they render for a phone run recorded with no strap. A run-detail line reading "heart rate covered 12 % of this run" is what makes the suppression legible instead of looking like data loss. Both trees belong to other lanes; the registry row is written and the data will be there when a reader is. **Web half closed 2026-09-03** — [decisions § 1088](../architecture/decisions.md); the mobile half was built independently in the same round. Run detail now resolves three states rather than one: coverage present with no average states the share and that it was too little for an average; a coverage of exactly `0` (sensor enabled, nothing delivered) gets its own sentence rather than "covered 0 %", and `hrCoveragePercent` floors a nonzero fraction at 1 % so rounding can never reach that reading; and an average that IS reported carries the share it was taken over whenever that is under 100 %, because 142 bpm over 62 % of a twelve-hour run is not that run's average. Absent stays *unmeasured* — a non-number, a non-finite one, or a fraction outside `0..1` keeps the old copy rather than reporting a duty cycle nobody measured. Three i18n keys in all seven catalogues, unit tests on the grading, three `hr-zones.spec.ts` cases on the rendered states. The CSV export still hands over `avg_bpm` unqualified — filed below. **Mobile half closed 2026-09-03** — [§ 1094](../architecture/decisions.md). `run_detail_screen.dart` now reads the key into three states: an average with no coverage record renders unchanged, a partly-covered average is qualified by an `HR coverage` cell (full coverage is not drawn — it qualifies nothing), and a SUPPRESSED average takes the `Avg HR` slot itself reading `12% covered`, because a reader looking for a missing number looks at the label it is missing from. `0%` is a real answer; an out-of-range, non-finite or non-numeric value is read as no record rather than clamped. Eight widget tests, seven ARBs. The web half is a separate lane's.
- [x] **`apps/watch_ios` writes `avg_bpm` with no coverage notion, and the registry row says so in prose only.** **CLOSED 2026-09-03** ([decisions § 1106](../architecture/decisions.md)) — on the truth, because the filing's second option cannot be written as filed. **There is no `source = 'watch_ios'`**: `SupabaseClient.kt` and `ContentView.syncRun` both put the literal `"watch"`, so the absence of `hr_coverage` is not self-addressing — a reader cannot tell an Apple Watch's workout-scoped average from a Wear run predating the key or recovered from a checkpoint that never carried it, the third case being one the registry row itself documents. **The measurement is filed, not taken, and the binding reason is structural**: watchOS hands a run to the phone through `WCSession.transferFile(_:metadata:)` and claim (6) of `scripts/check_watch_ios_source.mjs` reads both ends, so `hr_coverage` on the envelope fails the PR until `apps/mobile_ios/ios/Runner/WatchIngestBridge.swift` lifts it — a tree no lane owned this round. Secondarily, no Xcode here, and the two cheap approximations each measure something else (`HKStatistics`' start-to-end span credits a mid-run silence as covered; ticking on `didCollectDataOf` measures HealthKit's batching). What shipped: the scope statement on `HealthKitManager.summaryAverageBPM`, where a maintainer reads it before adding an assumed `1.0`, naming all three meanings of the absence; and a `MetadataRegistryTests` guard pinning that no watchOS source writes `hr_coverage` and that the statement stays. **The `docs/backend/metadata.md` replacement text is handed to integration** — that file belonged to another lane. Swift unbuilt (see the § 888 box above); both runnable watchOS guards pass. Original filing below. HealthKit's `HKLiveWorkoutBuilder` average is workout-scoped, so the watchOS figure has a genuinely better coverage story than the Wear one did — but it records no figure, so a reader holding two runs cannot tell which claim it is looking at. Either the same key from the watchOS side (its own measurement, not an assumed 1.0 — an assumed one would be a fabricated measurement, which is worse than none) or an explicit statement that absence on a `source = 'watch_ios'` run means workout-scoped. `apps/watch_ios/` belonged to no lane this round.
- [x] **The `noindex` claim in [§ 1084](../architecture/decisions.md) is a repo-level claim, not an observation of the edge.** **SETTLED 2026-09-05** ([decisions § 1266](../architecture/decisions.md)) — the claim is confirmed and stays repo-level, now as an observation. The filing's own command could never have run: `infra/envs/preview/main.tf:38` passes `aliases = []`, so the preview distribution is given no domain name, and `getent hosts preview.threkir.com` returns not-found while `threkir.com` resolves. Measured against prod instead — `GET https://threkir.com/share/run/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` answers **HTTP 200, `text/html`, 5,666 bytes, `server: AmazonS3`, `x-cache: Error from cloudfront`, and NO `robots` meta anywhere in the body**. The `custom_error_response` deletion is unapplied and the `noindex` is not on the wire. Content is not the stale half: the shell's `last-modified` is `2026-08-15T23:30:39Z` against `web@1.4.0` published 22 minutes earlier, so the bucket is current and the distribution config trails the Terraform. What remains is the apply, tracked by the standing no-credentials item below rather than here. Original filing below. The mapping is gone from the Terraform and the guard keeps it gone, but nothing here has seen a byte off CloudFront. Settles it against preview, no prod exposure, one command: `curl -sSi 'https://preview.threkir.com/share/run/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' | head -40` — a `404` status whose body carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` closes it; a 404 whose body is the plain S3 `/index.html` means the distribution still substitutes and the apply has not run. The same fetch answers the sibling question about whether `/api/coach*` now returns its JSON 404 rather than an HTML shell.
- [x] **Claim 10's derivation is per-role but the invoked set is repo-wide.** `check_infra_iam.mjs` compares BOTH deploy roles against the union of `aws lambda` verbs any workflow runs, so a verb only the production release calls would still be required on the preview role. That is correct today (release-web.yml runs the same steps down both branches) and would be wrong the moment a workflow deploys only one environment — the guard would then demand a verb preview never uses, and the fix would look like widening the role rather than narrowing the derivation. Pairing each verb with the environment its job targets is the honest version; `parseReleaseWorkflow` already reads that branch for claim 2. Not taken because it is unfalsifiable against today's workflows: there is no verb the two branches disagree about, so the stronger guard and the weaker one pass on exactly the same input. **Closed 2026-09-03** ([§ 1110](../architecture/decisions.md)). A verb is now attributed to the environments its job can assume a role for — the `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN_<ENV>` Secrets it names — narrowed by the step's own `if:` when that reads an output of the job's env branch; a verb run under an assumed role whose environment cannot be read FAILS rather than going unclaimed, and an environment a workflow deploys to that no role grants fails too. The filing's own objection is answered rather than waved past: because no committed workflow can produce a disagreeing input, the pin is a synthetic two-branch workflow carrying a verb only the production leg runs, and four tests separate the two derivations — the verb attributes to `prod` alone, the preview role passes without it, holding it on the preview role fails as standing privilege, and a prod role lacking it fails the other way. The union derivation passes the second and fails the third. `node scripts/check_infra_iam.mjs` reports 24 properties (16 invocations attributed across 2 environments); 77 unit tests; `npm run check:script-types` clean.

### Surfaced by the #789 round 37 web lane (2026-09-03)

- [x] **The four SPA-shell head injectors are four copies of one strip pipeline, and that is how the `js/bad-tag-filter` regex survived on `main` in triplicate.** **CLOSED 2026-09-04** ([decisions § 1114](../architecture/decisions.md)). Done in exactly the shape the filing named: `share/head_splice.ts` exports `stripStaleHeadSignals(html, signals)` and `spliceIntoHead(html, headTags)`, and each of the four injectors names the signals its own head supplies — all four for entity / route / run, `['title', 'social']` for recap, so the recap page keeps whatever canonical and JSON-LD the shell itself carries. The strips are applied in a fixed internal order whatever order a caller names them in, so two injectors selecting the same set cannot produce different bytes. **Behaviour is byte-identical**, measured rather than argued: a harness ran all four injectors plus `notFoundShell` over eleven shells — the three § 1086 end-tag spellings, an overlapping `<script>` open, an attribute-carrying block, a `</head\n>`, a headless document, the empty string, a minimal head, and the real `build/index.html` — and diffed 73,830 bytes of output before and after to zero. 14 new tests pin the two steps directly, including the one the filing exists to protect: a recap injection leaves the shell's canonical and `WebSite` node standing. `countHeadSignals` lives in the same module and reads the same pattern sources, so § 1115's shell guard cannot measure something other than what the strips act on. Prior state, kept because its measurement is still the record: **STILL OPEN. The measurement is right and the named cause is WRONG — re-diagnosed 2026-09-04 ([decisions § 1116](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Original filing below. Reproduced the artifact exactly as filed: a production build's `build/index.html` carries `<title>Threkir</title>` and nothing else of the four head signals, while `build/learn.html` carries a canonical and thirteen social meta tags. But **nothing overwrites anything** — `/` is never prerendered in the first place. `.svelte-kit/output/prerendered/pages/` holds `learn.html`, `learn/`, `sitemap.xml` and `app-capabilities.json` and **no `index.html`**, and `build/index.html` has the empty body and bare `kit.start(app, element)` of a generated fallback rather than a prerendered page's hydration payload. `src/routes/+page.ts` exports no `prerender` and there is no root `+layout.ts` to set one, so `/` is a client-rendered route like `/dashboard`. **Acting on the filed cause would take the site down**: `fallback: "200.html"` alone removes `build/index.html` from the output entirely, CloudFront's `default_root_object` then 403s on the site root, that 403 maps back to `/index.html` ([§ 1022](../architecture/decisions.md)), and all five share Lambdas' `build.mjs` fail at bundle time on a missing file. **The real fix is four changes across three trees and none is optional**: (1) `export const prerender = true` in `apps/web/src/routes/+page.ts`, so a landing page exists to write; (2) `fallback: "200.html"` in `apps/web/svelte.config.js`; (3) `spaShellPath` → `build/200.html` in each of the five `apps/web/lambda/{share-badge,share-entity,share-recap,share-route,share-run}/build.mjs`; (4) `response_page_path = "/200.html"` on the 403 `custom_error_response` in `infra/modules/web-stack/main.tf`. Fewer than all four either changes nothing (1 alone — the fallback still overwrites) or breaks the site (2 alone). Not taken in this lane because it owns only (2). Land the code first and the bucket holds `index.html` (now the landing page) beside `200.html`, while the live 403 still points at `/index.html` — so every deep link serves the LANDING page and hydrates a `/` payload on a different URL. Apply the infra first and the 403 points at a `200.html` that does not exist yet. The safe route is a three-step operator sequence: emit `200.html` WITHOUT prerendering `/` (changes 2 and 3 only, at which point `index.html` is still the shell and nothing moves), deploy, `terraform apply` change 4, then land change 1 in a second PR. Whoever takes this should confirm each step against the edge before the next, since no lane holds AWS credentials and none of it can be verified from the repo. Note also that since [§ 1167](../architecture/decisions.md) moved the default title into the root layout, the shell carries NO title either, so step 1 is now what restores a title to the site root as well. Original filing below. Measured on a production build of `apps/web`: `build/index.html` carries `<title>Threkir</title>` from `app.html`, the CSP meta, the icons and the module preloads — no `<link rel="canonical">`, no `og:`/`twitter:`/`description` meta and no `Organization` / `WebSite` JSON-LD. `src/routes/+page.svelte` builds all of it through `SeoHead` and `+page.ts` resolves the canonical host, and a genuinely prerendered sibling proves the mechanism works — `build/learn.html` carries both a canonical and an `og:title`. The cause is `svelte.config.js`'s `fallback: "index.html"`: adapter-static writes the prerendered pages and then generates the fallback **to the same path**, so the SPA shell replaces the landing page. [seo.md](../features/seo.md)'s render map states "`/` landing | prerendered | `SeoHead.svelte` + `+page.ts` | `Organization` + `WebSite`", which is what the source intends and not what the artifact contains. Three knock-ons: the site's most important indexable page has no canonical, no description and no structured data; the five share Lambdas embed that bare shell, which is why three of the four strips in each injector ([§ 1086](../architecture/decisions.md)) remove content the shell has never contained while their comments assert "adapter-static emits a default set that would render as duplicates"; and the same shell is what CloudFront serves for every 4xx ([§ 1022](../architecture/decisions.md)), so no deep link carries a canonical either. **Not fixable inside one tree**, which is why it is filed rather than taken: naming the fallback something else (`fallback: "200.html"`) frees `index.html` for the real landing page, but the share Lambdas' `build.mjs` all read `build/index.html` by name, the CloudFront error-response mapping and default root object are `infra/`, and the strips would become live again and want their tests. Owner trees: `apps/web/svelte.config.js` + `apps/web/lambda/*/build.mjs` + `infra/modules/web-stack/`.

### Surfaced by the #789 round 37 mobile lane (2026-09-03)

- [x] **Run detail's whole secondary-stat grid is gated on the run having GEOMETRY, so six geometry-independent stats vanish on a track-less run.** **CLOSED 2026-09-04** ([decisions § 1124](../architecture/decisions.md)). The filing is accurate. Every cell was read and classified against what it computes: the grid holds ten cell definitions (two of which — the partial-coverage and coverage-only heart-rate cells — are mutually exclusive, so at most nine ever render together), and exactly three need geometry: elevation gain and loss, gated on `_hasElevation`, which walks `run.track`, and the grade-adjusted pace, which is `gradeAdjustedPaceSecPerKm(run.track)`. The remaining seven come off the row or the metadata bag and are no less true of a run with no track; the filing's count of six is the same set with the two coverage variants counted once. Taken in the shape the filing named rather than by widening the condition: `_secondaryStatCells` builds the list first, each cell gates on its own datum, and the section renders only when the list is non-empty — so the padding collapses instead of drawing an empty frame, and the next cell added cannot inherit the bug. **One cell had no datum test at all and needed one added**: `_showCalories` is the universal `show_calories` pref, not a value check, and `estimateRunCalories` answers 0 for a distance it cannot use and for a product past the range both platforms share — so a run stopped before it moved would have reported "0 kcal" as the estimate the moment the grid stopped being hidden. It now gates on `_showCalories && calories > 0`, which is what web has always done. **Web was read for the same shape and does not have this bug** — its `/runs/[id]` key-stats grid has no geometry gate and every optional cell carries its own `{#if}` — but reading it surfaced the inverse defect on the canonical surface, filed at the end of this document: web renders elevation unconditionally, so a track-less run is told it climbed `0 m`. Five widget tests pin it (`run_detail_secondary_stats_test.dart`, mirrored to the iOS twin): a run with a track and full data renders all eight cells it carries data for; a track-less Health Connect-shaped import renders heart rate, steps, cadence, calories and age grade while the three geometry cells stay absent; a suppressed average still reports its § 1083 coverage with no track; a run with nothing renders exactly one `StatGrid` (the primary); and calories are absent rather than `0 kcal` when the estimate is unusable. Original filing below. `run_detail_screen.dart` wraps the grid in `if (run.track.length >= 2 || _hasElevation)`, and the cells inside it are elevation gain / loss and grade-adjusted pace (which do need geometry) plus calories, steps, cadence, average heart rate, HR coverage and age grade (which do not). A Health Connect import writes `avg_bpm` with no route (`health_connect_importer.dart` averages `HEART_RATE` samples in the workout window), and a manually-added run has no track at all, so those runs render no heart rate for a reason that has nothing to do with heart rate — which is the same class of illegible absence [§ 1094](../architecture/decisions.md) just closed one layer in. Widening the condition with six more disjuncts is the wrong shape; the durable fix is to build the cell list first and gate the block on `cells.isNotEmpty`, which is also what stops the next cell inheriting the bug. Not taken there because it predates that change, affects five other cells, and restructuring a 40-line widget block belongs in its own commit. Web's `/runs/[id]` should be read for the same shape. Owner tree: `apps/mobile_android/lib/screens/run_detail_screen.dart` (+ the iOS twin), `apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/`.

The reciprocal note — that Dart states the same rule natively, that the two client libraries differ in whether a failure is returned or thrown, and that `race_providers_test.dart` is what compares them — belongs in `provider_probe.ts`'s own header, which the mobile lane cannot edit. - [x] **The bounded settle cannot report when the awaiting zone is the fake one, which is row 5 of § 1093's own table.** `storeWritesSettled` arms its watchdog on `Zone.root` so the timer fires regardless of the caller's zone, but the error is DELIVERED through the awaiting zone's continuation — so a fake-zone `await` with no pump behind it still hangs to the runner's timeout, exactly as before. The measured case is a write queued from the fake zone and settled from the fake zone; a test in that state is wedged for a second reason anyway, which is why it was left. Closing it needs the report to reach the runner rather than the awaiter — `Zone.root.run` plus a `FlutterError.reportError`, or the test-package's own `registerException` — neither of which `core_models` can reach without a dependency it does not have and should not take. The honest version may be a thin `@visibleForTesting` reporter injected from the Flutter side. Owner tree: `packages/core_models/lib/src/store_write_chain.dart`, `apps/mobile_android/lib/`. **CLOSED 2026-09-04 ([decisions § 1130](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Premise verified first: at `c4b6137ec` a fake-zone write awaited from the fake zone with no pump prints `TimeoutException after 0:00:25.000000` and nothing else. The fix direction the filing named does NOT work and the measurement says so — in a wedged body a root-zone timer's `stderr.writeln` / `print` / `debugPrint` all surface immediately while `FlutterError.reportError` produces no output at all, because the test binding parks it in `_pendingExceptionDetails` until the body ends. So the diagnosis goes to `debugStoreWritesSettledSink`, the thin reporter injected from the Flutter side that the filing offered as the honest version, and it prints. Both deliveries are kept: completing the future serves an awaiter that can be resumed, the sink serves the runner when it cannot, and which happened is decided one root-zone second after the bound rather than in advance — § 1093 having measured that no property of the zone says. Both directions are pinned in `store_writes_settled_zone_test.dart`.

Of the filing's two options the re-grant is the one that was never available — `20270521_001`'s own header is the argument against it (the function trims LEADING in-zone points, so a three-point probe answers one bit and ~40 calls binary-search a victim's home to metre precision, on a PostgREST RPC no Edge Function rate limit covers), and a mobile surface wanting the method would be asking for the oracle back. So the method is deleted. The privacy-zone invariant is untouched: mobile's non-owner run surfaces already clip through `fetchClippedTrackForRun` (the `clip-public-track` Edge Function, service-role inside), and runs now have ONE client clipping path instead of one live and one dead. The three fail-closed assertions go with it; the fourth was rewritten rather than deleted — `public_route_screen must not call clipTrackForUser` would have become an assertion about a method nobody has, so it now forbids the run-bound `fetchClippedTrackForRun`, which is the claim it was making. Mirrored byte-for-byte to the iOS twin; `flutter test test/architecture_guards_test.dart` 234/234. **A second dead RPC caller in the same file was found by the § 1139 guard and deleted with it**: `ApiClient.publishPlanAsTemplate` calls `publish_plan_as_template`, which no migration has ever created — `TrainingService`'s copy was rewritten as the multi-table INSERT and says so, the api_client one was left behind. Both had zero callers. Two things the filing could not have known are filed below: `apps/mobile_android/CLAUDE.md`'s public_run_screen line and two `lib/` comments still name the deleted method. Original filing below. `20270521_001_heatmap_shadow_hidden_and_completion_race.sql` ends with `revoke execute on function clip_track_for_user(uuid, jsonb) from authenticated;` and no later migration re-grants it — measured on the local image, the ACL is `{postgres=X, service_role=X}`. `packages/api_client/lib/src/api_client.dart:4564` is the ONLY `.rpc('clip_track_for_user')` call anywhere in the repo (web reaches the clipping through `clip-public-track` and `clip_route_for_viewer` instead), it runs under the caller's own JWT, and it would now get a 42501 that its documented fail-closed `catch` swallows into `[]` — a silently empty track rather than an error. Nothing in `apps/mobile_android/lib/` calls it: every remaining mention is a comment saying *not* to (`global_segments_screen.dart`, `public_route_screen.dart`), and `architecture_guards_test.dart` carries three assertions pinning the method's fail-closed shape and one forbidding `public_route_screen` from using it. So this is guarded dead code whose grant was withdrawn four months ago. Not a privacy hole — the failure direction is closed — but the guard is protecting a method that can no longer work, and the next reader will believe it does. The durable fix is to delete the method and its guards (the twin invariant makes it two trees), or, if a mobile surface is meant to have it, to re-grant `authenticated` by name in a migration that says why. Owner trees: `packages/api_client/`, `apps/mobile_android/test/` + the iOS twin — not this lane's.

The durable fix is the shape `check_migration_function_revoke_noop.mjs` already has for the negative direction: replay the migration text per function signature (create / drop / grant / revoke in order), derive the stated ACL, and fail when a registered (routine, role) pair is not in it. That half was the one worth having first — a mean over three minutes of a twelve-hour run saved as the run's average is a wrong number reaching run detail, the coach context and the export, where a missing coverage figure is only an unanswered question. Every unusable input keeps today's behaviour (`coveredSeconds` nil until the `HKWorkoutSession` actually starts — unmeasured, not zero; non-finite and non-positive clocks pass the mean through), because on an uncompilable sensor path a measurement that failed toward zero would delete a good `avg_bpm` on every run rather than on the runs it is about.   ```sql

  alter table public.jobs
    add constraint jobs_kind_chk
    check (

        'map_match', 'token_refresh', 'strava_event', 'photo_process',
        'notification_email', 'lifecycle_email', 'safety_email', 'web_push',

  create or replace function enqueue_export_blob_reap()

  language sql

  set search_path = public

    insert into public.jobs (kind, payload, max_attempts)
    select 'export_blob_reap', '{}'::jsonb, 3

Neither candidate fix in the filing was taken. Naming the three contexts in branch protection puts a path-filtered required check on every PR (it never starts on a web-only diff, so it never reports) and lives in a setting no lane can read, so its removal would leave no trace in the repo. Moving the three job bodies into `ci.yml` would have carried the `stack:` matrix with them, and `scripts/check_infra_coverage.mjs` reads that matrix and the `terraform fmt` invocations out of `terraform.yml` by path — the fix would have broken the § 890 mechanism it depends on. Instead `terraform.yml` is now `on: workflow_call` only and `ci.yml` CALLS it from a `terraform` job that is in the gate's `needs:` list. A called workflow's job results fan into the calling job, so that one entry covers every job the file gains later; `check_ci_diagnostics.mjs` rule 3 now counts 33 jobs and fails if the entry is dropped (demonstrated); and actionlint, already in the gated `workflow-lint` job, fails `ci.yml` if `terraform.yml` loses its `workflow_call` trigger or is deleted (both demonstrated) — so the wiring cannot be severed from either end without a red. The path filter moved onto a new `infra` output of the `changes` job, and `pull-requests: write` went with the triggers (no step posts anything). What is still NOT verified from here is the branch-protection setting itself; the claim this closes is the narrower one, that the Terraform checks are inside the context branch protection is documented to require. Original filing below. The `CI gate` job in `ci.yml` `needs:` 32 jobs and none of them is from `terraform.yml` — nor could one be, since `needs:` is scoped to its own workflow. `ci.yml` runs no `terraform` command at all (its three matches are prose in comments, which is what [§ 1021](../architecture/decisions.md) already measured). So `fmt (whole tree)`, `validate (<stack>)` and `Trivy IaC scan` are advisory rows unless branch protection separately requires them, which no lane can read and which this repo's own CLAUDE.md contradicts: "the single required **CI gate** status check". This is [§ 764](../architecture/decisions.md)'s hazard exactly — "a job outside the list has a red that blocks nothing and reads as one more green row among thirty" — one workflow over, and it is worse here because `terraform.yml` is also path-filtered to `infra/**`, so on most PRs the rows are not merely non-blocking but absent. `infra-guards` (the three `.mjs` guards) IS in the gate and does block, so what is unprotected is precisely `fmt`, `validate` and Trivy. Two candidate fixes, and the choice is the owner's: add the terraform jobs' equivalents to `ci.yml` behind the existing `changes` filter so the gate can wait for them, or add them to branch protection by name and accept that a path-filtered required check blocks every PR that does not touch `infra/`. Owner tree: `.github/workflows/` + branch protection.

- [x] **Every prerendered page ships TWO `<title>` tags, and the first one is `Threkir`.** **CLOSED 2026-09-04** ([decisions § 1167](../architecture/decisions.md)). The measurement was reproduced exactly as filed on a fresh production build — 15 of 16 built HTML files carried two `<title>` elements, `build/index.html` the only exception — and the fix is the shape the filing named, after settling the premise it flagged as unmeasured. **That premise was wrong**: Svelte 5 does NOT concatenate, it dedupes. `Renderer.set_title` in `svelte/src/internal/server/renderer.js` keeps one title per document by depth-first path comparison, letting the deepest component's displace every ancestor's, so a default in the root layout's `<svelte:head>` is REPLACED by a page's own rather than reproduced beside it — measured by planting a sentinel default and finding it in none of the fifteen prerendered pages. What the dedupe cannot see is a literal in `app.html`, because that is not a component. So the literal is gone and the default now lives in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. Measured after: every prerendered page carries exactly one title, its own; `build/index.html` carries none. **The titleless shell is deliberate, not an oversight** — adapter-static's fallback renders no components, so no layout default can reach it, and the alternative that keeps it titled (moving the literal AFTER `%sveltekit.head%` so the page's own comes first) ships a spec-forbidden duplicate on fifteen pages and plants a trap for § 1116's landing page. Both consequences are filed below: the `spa_shell_head_signals.test.ts` re-measurement it forces, and the site root's raw HTML having no title until `/` is prerendered. Five assertions in `apps/web/src/lib/seo/document_title.test.ts` pin the source and artifact halves, each proved non-vacuous — the fifth added after the replacement COMMENT in `app.html` named `%sveltekit.head%` in prose and SvelteKit substituted the whole head into the comment, leaving the CSP meta inert and the literal placeholder standing as raw text in `<head>` while every head-shape assertion still passed ([§ 1169](../architecture/decisions.md)). Original filing below. Measured 2026-09-04 on a production build of `apps/web`: 15 of the 16 built HTML files carry two `<title>` elements — the only one that does not is `build/index.html`, the SPA fallback. `src/app.html` writes a literal `<title>Threkir</title>` before `%sveltekit.head%`, and every prerendered page then contributes its own through `<svelte:head>`, so `build/learn/couch-to-5k.html` reads `<title>Threkir</title><title>Couch to 5K: your first month — Threkir</title>`. Per the HTML spec the document title is the **first** `title` element, so a raw fetch — every non-JS crawler, every social unfurler, and the browser tab until hydration replaces it — gets the generic site name on all twelve `/learn` pages, which are the only surfaces this app deliberately prerenders **for** indexing ([learn.md](../features/learn.md), [decisions § 161](../architecture/decisions.md)). Not fixed in the round that measured it because the obvious repair is wrong in both directions: deleting `app.html`'s title leaves the SPA fallback (the site root and every deep-link 403 body, [§ 1022](../architecture/decisions.md)) with no title at all and shows the raw URL in the tab, and it would also kill the one strip in each share-Lambda injector that currently has work to do ([§ 1115](../architecture/decisions.md)). The durable shape is a default title emitted from the root layout's `<svelte:head>` rather than from the template, so a page's own title replaces it instead of following it — which needs a measurement first, because Svelte's SSR `<svelte:head>` concatenates rather than dedupes and a layout title may simply reproduce the pair one level down. Owner trees: `apps/web/src/app.html` + `apps/web/src/routes/+layout.svelte`.

### Surfaced by the #789 round 38 mobile run-detail lane (2026-09-04)

- [x] **Web's run-detail renders elevation unconditionally, so every track-less run is told it climbed `0 m`.** **CLOSED 2026-09-04** ([decisions § 1164](../architecture/decisions.md)). **All four claims verified against the file before acting; all four held.** The elevation cell now gates on the samples rather than on the answer — `elevationSourceTrack` returns the track when any point carries an `ele` and null otherwise, `realElevationGain` is null when it does, and the cell is absent. The opposite error is pinned separately: a genuinely flat run over a track that DID record altitude still renders its real `0 m`, because suppressing that reports a measurement as an absence. `hasElevation` at line 1076 was NOT reused — it reads `baseTrack`, which prefers the map-matched track, and the gain is computed from `run.track`; gating one track's sum on another track's samples is a second bug waiting. `totalSteps` and `avgCadence` now require a datum (matching mobile's `> 0` gates), a fractional step count truncates the way mobile's `_steps` does, and a reported `cadence_spm` that rounds away to zero claims nothing rather than falling through to the pedometer count — mobile returns the rounded reading and hides the tile, so falling through would make the two platforms disagree about one run. The count was not repaired but deleted: `keyStatsCount`'s hand-maintained `6 +` is replaced by a derived `keyStats` list of `{label, value}` cells that the template renders with an `{#each}`, and `showActivityFiller` reads `keyStats.length` — so item 4 cannot recur, and a cell added later cannot desynchronise a count that is the list's own length. Gating predicates extracted to `$lib/runs/key_stats` with 13 unit tests; the elevation rule itself stays called on the page per § 1004's guard, and two further guard cases pin the `{#each}` and the filler's read of `.length`. No new i18n keys. Original filing below. `apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte:804` derives `realElevationGain = run?.track ? Math.round(computeElevationGain(run.track)) : 0` and line 1676 renders it as a key stat with no `{#if}` at all. A manual entry and a summary import have no track, and a track carrying no `ele` sums to 0 the same way, so three different states — no track, altitude never recorded, and a genuinely flat run — all render the identical `0 m`. That is the fabricated-zero half of the class [§ 1124](../architecture/decisions.md) just closed on mobile, where the cell already gated on `_hasElevation` and is absent rather than zero. The change is to gate the cell on the same test mobile uses (`run?.track?.some((p) => p.ele != null)`, which the file already computes as `hasElevation` at line 1076 for the elevation chart) and to decrement `keyStatsCount`'s always-rendered `6` accordingly. Two smaller instances of the same shape sit beside it and are worth taking in the same pass: `totalSteps` accepts any `number`, so a stored `steps: 0` renders as `0` where mobile requires `> 0` (no writer in this repo emits it, but the metadata bag has no schema and a third-party import could); and `avgCadence`'s `Math.round((totalSteps / (movingSeconds / 60)) || 0)` returns `0` rather than `null` for that same zero, so the run then also claims `0 spm`. `keyStatsCount`'s own comment is separately wrong today — it counts Calories among the six that "never hide" while the template gates it on `showCalories && estimatedCalories > 0`, so the odd/even activity-filler flips the wrong way whenever the estimate is unusable or the pref is off. Not taken here: the round-38 mobile run-detail lane owns no path under `apps/web/`. Owner tree: `apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte`.

- [x] **A night the worker is down still orphans export bytes, and the reaper cannot reach them afterwards.** [§ 1144](../architecture/decisions.md) schedules `enqueue-export-blob-reap` at 04:13, ten minutes ahead of `cleanup-stale-export-blobs` at 04:23, so in the normal case the Storage-API erasure happens before the row delete and the sweep finds nothing left to orphan. The lead is best-effort: if the worker is down (or the job fails its three attempts) the sweep still deletes the `storage.objects` rows at 04:23, and the bytes then join the pile [§ 1049](../architecture/decisions.md) measured — unreachable by any Storage-API reaper, because list reads the rows that are gone. This is a NEW orphan created after the reaper shipped, distinct from the residue box above, which is about the pile that already exists. Three candidate fixes and the choice is the owner's. (a) Stop the sweep deleting `exports` rows and rely wholly on the worker: closes the leak, but trades away the unconditional removal of reachability that is the one thing SQL can guarantee, so a long worker outage leaves week-old archives listable. (b) Have the sweep skip a row whose object the reaper has not yet had a chance at — needs the sweep to know the reap's outcome, which is a status read across tiers. (c) An S3 lifecycle rule on the `exports` bucket prefix as a backstop, which also erases the existing pile and is the same operator action the § 1049 residue box already needs. (c) subsumes both piles and is the recommendation. Owner tree: `apps/backend/supabase/migrations/` or an operator + `docs/ops/`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1172](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Option (a), and the objection this entry raised against it is measurably false: the trade named was "a long worker outage leaves week-old archives listable", but the `exports` bucket carries NO `storage.objects` policies (`20270602_001`, deliberately) and `20260816_001` had already carved `exports/` out of the owner-folder SELECT on `runs` — an export is reachable through the server-minted 10-minute signed URL and nothing else, so the row delete was removing a reachability nobody had. The same migration answers § 1144's open question about the legacy `runs/{uid}/exports/*` leg: the enqueue now derives one prefix-scoped job per user who still has a legacy archive, so the set empties itself, and the singleton guard is per-PAYLOAD. Two cross-tier Go guards, both negative-controlled: the `jsonb_build_object` keys against the handler's payload struct, and a replay of every migration's `cron.schedule`/`unschedule` proving the sweep is not scheduled again. Not done and filed below: an ALERT for a worker down long enough to overrun retention, which needs the post-condition check to move, and `docs/backend/api_database.md`'s cron table still lists the sweep as scheduled — both outside this lane's tree.
- [x] **`migration_locks.md`'s "both halves in one migration" advice and `check_migration_online_safety.mjs` both treat a same-file `NOT VALID` + `VALIDATE` as online, and it is not.** Measured this round ([decisions § 1148](../architecture/decisions.md)): `apps/backend/scripts/apply-pending-migrations.sh` applies each migration as `begin;` … `commit;` (it has to — the ledger row commits atomically with the SQL), and `migration_locks.md` itself asserts the CLI wraps a file the same way, which is its stated reason `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` errors as apply-time DDL. A lock taken by DDL is held until the transaction ends, so in a file holding `drop constraint` + `add … not valid` + `validate constraint` the `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` from the `drop` is still held during the `validate` scan; `VALIDATE`'s `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` is subsumed by it, never a downgrade. Same-file, the two-step and the single-step take the identical lock for the identical duration. Two owners. **(1)** `docs/backend/migration_locks.md` § CHECK constraints says "putting both in one migration is still far better than the single-step form (the `NOT VALID` add doesn't scan, and the `VALIDATE` uses the weaker lock)" — the parenthesis is true statement-by-statement and false as applied, and the sentence should say the split must be across MIGRATIONS to buy anything, which the same section's "ideally a later migration" already hints at. `20270603_001`'s own comment carries the same wrong claim about `jobs`, and § 1148 corrects it for the record rather than editing an applied migration. **(2)** `apps/backend/scripts/check_migration_online_safety.mjs` grades the statement shape, so a same-file two-step is exactly the shape it looks for: it passes a migration taking the lock it exists to prevent, on a table its own `GUARDED_TABLES` names. The durable fix is to grade the pair by FILE — a `VALIDATE` in the same file as the `ADD` (or after a `DROP CONSTRAINT`) on a guarded table is a violation, not a compliance — with the existing grandfather-by-name list absorbing the shipped history. That is [§ 764](../architecture/decisions.md)'s hazard one tier over: a guard whose green means less than its name says. Not taken here: `docs/backend/` and `apps/backend/scripts/` were both outside this lane, which held exactly one migration file. Owner tree: `docs/backend/migration_locks.md` + `apps/backend/scripts/check_migration_online_safety.mjs` (+ its `.test.mjs`). **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1180](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Both owners done. The doc now says the split must be across migration FILES and its lock-reference row for `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` carries the qualifier; the guard walks each file in order and reports a second violation kind, `same_txn_validate`. The rule is BROADER than the filing proposed, and the breadth is load-bearing: keying it on constraint DDL alone would have missed `20261127_001`, which validates after an `ADD COLUMN` — the lock is the table's, not the constraint's. Any earlier `ALTER TABLE` action other than another `VALIDATE`, plus `CREATE INDEX` / `CREATE TRIGGER` on the same table, escalates; DML does not, because `ROW EXCLUSIVE` and `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` do not conflict. Within one `ALTER TABLE` the action order is irrelevant, since the statement takes the strongest lock any action needs. **The filing's parenthetical about `GRANDFATHER_CUTOFF` is stale** — [§ 775](../architecture/decisions.md) retired the cutoff for a name list before this filing was written, and the guard's own tests already pinned that; no cutoff exists to regress. 28 `same_txn_validate` entries across eleven files join the 32 `blocking_add` ones, and `kind` is now part of the allowlist key so one exemption cannot cover the other class. The guard's own suite had pinned the wrong verdict in as many words ("passes a NOT VALID jobs_kind_chk widening"); that test is inverted and nine more cover the new kind.

The block is at `CLAUDE.md` under `.github/workflows/`, and reads today: `ci.yml             → the same 33 CI jobs run on every PR and push to main` / `                       (no PR-only/push-only split); the single required status` / `                       check is the "CI gate" aggregator that needs: all of them`. No guard reads the number in `CLAUDE.md`, which is why it drifted unnoticed through every round that added a job. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1217](../architecture/decisions.md)).** **The filing was already stale**: the round-38 merge this branch was cut from (`8a414ff79`) had already replaced 33 with 34 in `CLAUDE.md`, without ticking the box. Re-measured rather than trusted — `parseJobKeys` over `.github/workflows/ci.yml` returns **34** job keys and `parseNeeds(text, 'ci-gate')` returns **33**, so 34 is right. The residual falsehood the round-38 fix left is the next clause: with 34 jobs stated, an aggregator that "needs: all of them" is off by one, because it cannot wait on itself. Now reads "which needs: every one of the other 33 — among them `terraform`, a caller job whose real work is terraform.yml, whose own jobs could never be named in a needs: list (decisions § 1149)". - [x] **Terraform added outside `infra/` would be format-checked, validated, Trivy-scanned and CI-triggered by nothing at all.** Pre-existing, and surfaced rather than created by [§ 1149](../architecture/decisions.md): the new `infra` output of `ci.yml`'s `changes` job inherits the old `terraform.yml` trigger's path list (`infra/`, `.trivyignore`, the workflow file), so a `.tf` file under some other tree does not even start the job — exactly as the trigger did not. `scripts/check_infra_coverage.mjs` cannot report it either: `terraformDirs(INFRA_DIR)` walks `infra/` and nothing else, so its claim "every directory holding `.tf` is in the matrix" is scoped to a tree the file is not in. Write the key only when the claim's `coverage` is non-nil: an assumed figure is a fabricated one. **(3)** `docs/backend/metadata.md`'s `hr_coverage` row: add `apps/watch_ios` to the Writers column and REPLACE the "**Wear OS only, and the absence is three-way ambiguous**" passage — after this lands, a `source = 'watch'` run with no `hr_coverage` is still ambiguous, but the population changes (an Apple-Watch run whose `HKWorkoutSession` never started joins the Wear cases, and a normal Apple-Watch run leaves them). That row belonged to no lane this round and belongs to whichever lane owns `docs/backend/` next. **Secondary, and it is a real gate rather than a formality:** the accumulator has never run — no Xcode here — and its one silent failure mode is reading blank on a device, which would write `hr_coverage: 0.0` on every run. The local suppression already fails closed against that (nil is unmeasured, not zero), but the KEY is a durable record and wants a simulator or device run before it is written, not just a green compile. (b) The secondary gate stands unchanged: still no Xcode here, the accumulator has never executed, and a blank timestamp source on a device would send `hr_coverage: 0.0` on every run — the non-nil gate does not catch that, because zero is a measurement. - [x] **"Discard" on the Wear crash-recovery prompt destroys the run's only durable record on one tap, with no confirmation.** Found while closing [§ 1154](../architecture/decisions.md) and deliberately not widened into it. `discardCheckpoint` calls `checkpoints.clear()` immediately; the checkpoint is, by [§ 1107](../architecture/decisions.md)'s own words, "the run's only durable record" when the queue does not hold the run. That is the house `destructive-action-without-confirm` anti-pattern the `/ux-hunt` loop exists for, on the most consequential button in the app, read by a runner who has just crashed out of a recording. It is **worse since § 1154** rather than merely unchanged: while the queue is unreadable, Discard is now the only enabled control on the screen, so a runner who wants their run and finds "Save it" greyed out has exactly one thing left to press. The fix is the Wear idiom used elsewhere in this tree — a two-press confirm, or the `undo_queue` deferred-commit shape web and mobile already share (decisions § 523) — not a dialog, which does not fit the takeover.
