The shape taken is the estate's own, from `apps/custom_watch`'s FACTORY ERASE (§ 378) and PAIR PHONE (§ 432): arm, announce the arm, commit on a second press, lapse on a timer. New pure `ui/ConfirmGuard.kt` (`confirmPress` + `CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS`) with 7 host-JVM tests, the chip relabelling to `discard_confirm` and showing `discard_stake` while armed, both strings in all seven catalogues, and `RecoveryPromptDisclosureTest` extended to pin that the press is graded through `confirmPress`, that `onDiscardRecovery()` appears exactly ONCE in the whole takeover, and that the arm lapses. Verified by breaking it: reverting the chip to `onClick = onDiscardRecovery` fails the new test. Full `:app:testDebugUnitTest` green afterwards — 741 tests, 0 failures.
- [x] **`RotaryScrollWiringTest` pairs rotary scrolls with a `requestFocus` by IDENTIFIER, so a correctly-wired list under any other variable name fails the build.** Found by hitting it: [§ 1154](../architecture/decisions.md)'s new scrolling takeover named its `FocusRequester` `recoveryRotary` and the guard failed, counting 4 `rotaryScrollable(` call sites against 3 matches of the literal regex `rotaryFocus\.requestFocus\(\)`. Renaming to the file's own idiom was the right call for that change and is what shipped, but the guard's claim — "each rotary list needs its FocusRequester focused" — is about the PAIRING, not about a variable name, and as written it also passes vacuously in the opposite direction: two `rotaryScrollable` sites both focusing the same requester count 2 against 2. Widen the second regex to `\w+\.requestFocus\(\)` and, better, match each `rotaryScrollable(...)`'s own `focusRequester = <name>` argument against a `<name>.requestFocus()` in the same composable, so the count is a pairing rather than two tallies. Low priority, no live defect — filed because the next person to add a rotary list will lose the same twenty minutes. Owner tree: `apps/watch_wear/android/app/src/test/kotlin/com/runapp/watchwear/RotaryScrollWiringTest.kt`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1205](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Taken the better of the two options the filing offered — the pairing, not the widened regex. `RunWatchApp.kt` is split into top-level functions (the scope a `remember { FocusRequester() }` lives in), each `.rotaryScrollable(` argument list is brace-matched, its own `focusRequester = <name>` read, and that name required to be created and focused in the same function with no two call sites sharing one. A shared `RotaryWiring` helper replaces the duplicate count-vs-count check `RecoveryPromptDisclosureTest` carried, so the takeover cannot drift back to the identifier form on its own. Not weakened: the total call-site floor stays, and every call site must fall inside a parsed function or the guard fails rather than silently exempting it. Measured on all three shapes — the renamed requester passes the new guard and fails the old one (4 against 3); deleting `RoutePickerScreen`'s `requestFocus()` fails the new guard NAMING that function; and two lists sharing one requester fail the new guard while passing the old one at 5 against 5.
- [x] **Three rails break a tie between two future long runs on the same date three different ways, and one of the three is an invalid comparator.** Found while measuring the `plan_replan` firmware port for [decisions § 1163](../architecture/decisions.md); out of scope for that lane, which owned neither web `training/` nor `apps/mobile_android/lib/plan_replan.dart`. `apps/web/src/lib/training/plan_replan.ts:142` sorts `futureLongRuns` with `(a, b) => (a.scheduledDate < b.scheduledDate ? -1 : 1)` — a comparator that **never returns 0**, so it is not a valid ordering and `Array.prototype.sort`'s stability does not apply to the equal pair; V8's TimSort may put either first. The Dart twin `plan_replan.dart:174` uses `compareTo` (correct, returns 0) but `List.sort` is UNSTABLE, so its tie order is also arbitrary. The firmware `plan_replan.rs:169` scans with a strict `<` and keeps the FIRST encountered in week-then-workout order, which is deterministic and is the only one of the three that is. The input is a plan carrying two non-past, non-taper `kind == 'long'` workouts on the same `scheduled_date` — a double long-run day, or a plan edited to move one — and the consequence is that the make-up distance is added to a different session on each platform. Fix: make web's comparator return 0 on equality and give both web and Dart an explicit deterministic tiebreak (workout id, or the input index the way `routine_history` and `readiness` already do), then pin it in the mirror suites. Pre-existing at port time; not caused by any of the commits § 1163 examined. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1200](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Fixed on all three rails, but two thirds of the diagnosis measured out differently. V8's TimSort with that comparator was measured over 260,000 random arrays — 2 to 570 elements, 1 to 5 distinct dates, including shapes built to force galloping — and never once disagreed with a valid stable sort, so the web rail was accidentally deterministic rather than arbitrary; every comparison path in TimSort reads "not less than" as "go right", and the descending-run detector that would break stability refuses to open on an equal pair. Dart is where the divergence was real, and for a reason the filing did not name: `List.sort` is an insertion sort up to 33 elements and a dual-pivot quicksort past it, so it was stable BY LIST SIZE — measured over 20,000 random cases, zero divergences at 33 or fewer and 12,024 past it. `plan_weeks.week_index` has no ceiling and `plan_workouts` no per-week cap, so 34 future long runs is reachable. Both scripting rails now SCAN for the earliest rather than sorting, which is the shape the firmware already had and needs no appeal to any sort's stability — deliberately not the `routine_history` / `readiness` house shape, which those two need because they consume a whole ordered list where this reads only `[0]`. Pinned twice on each of the three suites: the two-workout case, and a 40-element case past Dart's insertion-sort threshold.

Two reasons it was not taken, both real: the Monkey C field is a STREAMING estimator with no batch entry point that grades a whole track, so the fixture would have to be fed sample by sample through `updateGrade` and the result read off `gapPace` — a different test, not a mirror — and there is no Connect IQ SDK on this machine, so anything written there is source-level only and unexecuted (the same caveat § 992 recorded). The firmware's own `GapEstimator` has the same shape and could carry the streaming form first, which would give the Monkey C rail something to mirror rather than invent. Not owned by the lane that filed this. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1201](../architecture/decisions.md)).** The streaming objection turned out not to bind: `GradeTracker.onSample` re-anchors on exactly the condition the three batch graders close a segment on, so the fixture is fed to a real tracker one sample at a time and each closed window credited its horizontal length times the factor the tracker's own grade earns it. That reduction returns 311 s/km against a true 302.611 s/km, a 2.77 % cost — the same two figures § 1160 recorded for the other three rails, reached through this rail's own window, clamp and Minetti fit. The eight fixture constants are declared with the same names the TS and Rust rails use and were read through `check_watch_wire_vectors.mjs`'s own `mcConst` regex: all four rails produce byte-identical joined specs. **The Monkey C is still unexecuted** — no Connect IQ SDK here — so it sits BELOW *host-tested* on `quality_standards.md`'s ladder; what was executed is a faithful transliteration on the host, re-run under emulated 32-bit floats (Monkey C's default `Float` width) and reporting the same 311 with 0.448 of rounding headroom. - [x] **Switching the map matcher to OSRM silently strips `ele`, `ts` and `bpm` from every matched track, and three web surfaces read the matched track by preference.** Measured while closing [§ 1164](../architecture/decisions.md). `OSRMMatcher.Match` in `apps/job_worker/internal/matcher_osrm.go:204` builds its output as `TrackPoint{Lng: c[0], Lat: c[1]}` off the response geometry — the three optional fields on `internal.TrackPoint` (`ele`, `ts`, `bpm`) are dropped, because OSRM's `/match` returns coordinates and nothing else. That is invisible today only because the shipped default is `PassthroughMatcher`, which copies the input points verbatim; the swap is one env var (`OSRM_URL` in `apps/job_worker/main.go:347`), and the trigger in migration `20260609_001` enqueues a `map_match` job for EVERY run with a `track_url`, so the day that variable is set every run's matched track loses its altitude, its timestamps and its heart rate. `/runs/[id]` then degrades in three places at once, because `baseTrack` prefers `matchInfo.track` whenever it has two points: `hasElevation` goes false and the whole Elevation Profile section DISAPPEARS from runs that recorded altitude (`+page.svelte:1117`, `:1749`); `elevations` collapses to all-zero behind it; and `RunMap`'s pace heatmap falls back to the flat single-line render, since it gates on `hasTrackTimestamps(track)` (`RunMap.svelte:541`) over the same preferred track. Two candidate fixes and they are not equivalent. The durable one is in the worker: OSRM's `/match` returns a `tracepoints` array that indexes each input point onto the matched geometry, so the matcher can carry `ele`/`ts`/`bpm` across rather than discard them, and every consumer keeps working with no client change. The narrower one is on the page: source the elevation chart from whichever track actually recorded altitude (`elevationSourceTrack` from `$lib/runs/key_stats` already answers that) and pass `onhover` only when that track IS `baseTrack` — the linked cursor is an index into the track the map draws, and the two index spaces are different lengths once the geometry is re-sampled, so wiring it across them would point the map marker at the wrong place rather than at nothing. Not taken in § 1164's lane: the worker is another tree, and the page-side half needs the index-space decision above plus a matched-track e2e fixture that does not exist yet (nothing under `tests-e2e/` plants a `matched_track_url` with a Storage object). Owner tree: `apps/job_worker/internal/matcher_osrm.go`, or `apps/web/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1170](../architecture/decisions.md)).** The durable half, in the worker. `matchChunk` now pairs `tracepoints[i]` with `chunk[i]` — the array holds one entry per INPUT coordinate in input order — moves the position onto the snapped `location` and leaves `ele` / `ts` / `bpm` alone; the route geometry is no longer read, so `overview=false`, and `tidy` is switched OFF because every point it drops is now a lost heart-rate sample rather than a tidier line. A mis-indexed `tracepoints` array, an absent one, and a `null` entry each carry the affected points through RAW rather than dropping them, which makes `Match` length-preserving: one output point per input point, in order. The now-unreachable `len(out) < 2` skip is gone. The page-side half is not re-filed — length preservation is exactly the index-space property it was blocked on, and `hasElevation` / `hasTrackTimestamps` are both true again over `baseTrack` with no client change. The matched-track e2e fixture the filing named as missing is still missing and is filed below.

- [ ] **`gitleaks` and CodeQL run on every PR and block no merge, because the required check can only wait for jobs in its own workflow.** **gitleaks half CLOSED 2026-09-05** ([decisions § 1264](../architecture/decisions.md)); the CodeQL half stays open and is the OWNER's, sharpened below. **The filing's stated obstacle to folding gitleaks does not exist.** "Both upload SARIF to the Security tab" is true of `security.yml` and false of `gitleaks.yml`: read at the pinned SHA `e0c47f4`, none of `gitleaks-action`'s four source files contains `code-scanning`, `sarifs` or `security-events` — it writes a job summary, uploads a SARIF ARTIFACT this repo already disables, and `process.exit(1)`s on a detection. So its exit status was the entire signal and nothing waited for it. It is now CALLED from an ungated `gitleaks` job in `ci.yml` named in the `CI gate`'s `needs:` (the § 1149 shape), measured at 18 s against a gate critical path of 18 m 34 s; the unexercised `security-events: write` scope is gone and `GITLEAKS_ENABLE_COMMENTS` is off rather than failing a POST `pull-requests: read` cannot authorise. **The CodeQL half was wrong about what a fold would buy, and is not taken.** `github/codeql-action/analyze` at the pinned SHA declares 18 inputs and none is a severity threshold, so an alert never turns the job red — folding would gate on the analysis COMPLETING, not on what it found. And `getAnalysisKey()` is `${workflowPath}:${jobName}` resolved from the RUN's workflow, so a fold re-keys all four analyses at once, the exact churn `security.yml`'s header records being burned by. **The ask for the owner is therefore narrower than the filing's:** in branch-protection / rulesets, ADD the code-scanning results requirement (the `CodeQL` check run, not the four `analyze` job names) at whatever severity threshold is wanted, and leave the required-status-check set at exactly `CI gate` — which now covers gitleaks. Nothing in this tree can read or make that change. Original filing below. Branch protection requires exactly one context, the `CI gate` aggregator in `ci.yml`, and a `needs:` entry is scoped to its own workflow — so `gitleaks.yml`'s scan and `security.yml`'s four CodeQL legs are advisory in practice, however red. That is [§ 775](../architecture/decisions.md)'s shape, and the repo has already applied the fix twice by FOLDING the workflow in ([§ 771](../architecture/decisions.md) for the bundle budget, [§ 862](../architecture/decisions.md) for env-isolation). Neither of these two folds the same way: both upload SARIF to the Security tab, `security.yml` deliberately runs Trivy at `exit-code: '0'` and reports rather than blocks ([§ 8703 region](../architecture/decisions.md)), and CodeQL's own triggers were deliberately widened to every commit for Scorecard's SAST check. That is a repo-settings change no file in this tree can make, which is why it is filed rather than taken. Measure before deciding: a secret committed to a PR today produces a red `gitleaks` row and a mergeable PR. The [§ 1191](../architecture/decisions.md) guard reads the STRUCTURED-DATA cell only; widening it to the mode cell means teaching it what each route file exports, which is a different and larger claim than the one that kept drifting. Owner tree: `docs/features/seo.md`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1193](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Taken further than filed, because the reason the cell could not be right is that ONE row described TWO routes whose modes differ. `/learn` and `/learn/category/[category]` now have a row each, so every cell states something about a single named file, and the § 1191 guard is widened from the structured-data cell to the whole row: the mode cell must name `prerendered` exactly when the loader exports `prerender = true` and `entries()` exactly when it exports `entries`; the head-owner cell must name `<svelte:head>` exactly when the page uses one and must name the JSON-LD builder the page actually calls and only that one (which also earned `/learn/[slug]` its `buildGuideJsonLd`, previously unnamed). All three cells are now derived from route source, so still no build is needed and the case binds in `test-web`. Proved on five planted drifts: both directions of the `entries()` claim, a head-owner cell that stops naming its builder, and the two historical structured-data drifts.

- [x] **`notFoundShell` strips the shell's `description` and social meta and puts none back, which is deliberate and pinned nowhere.** `entity_spa_shell.ts` routes its 404 body through `injectEntityHead`, which strips all four signals, while the head it splices is a `<title>` plus `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. That is the documented intent — its own comment says a page saying the entity is GONE must carry nothing about it, whatever the shell arrived with — and it is the one deliberate exception to the rule [§ 1190](../architecture/decisions.md) states, that an injector strips exactly what its own head replaces. No test states it: `entity_spa_shell.test.ts` covers the noindex and the malformed-shell fallback, but nothing asserts that a shell arriving WITH a description leaves without one. It costs nothing today because the shell carries none, which is exactly the condition under which § 1190's two defects hid. A case feeding `notFoundShell` a shell carrying all four signals and asserting the output carries only the title and the robots meta would make the exception a statement rather than a silence. Measured: adding a `<link rel="canonical">` to the 404 head leaves 14 of the 15 cases green. The new case counts what the document carries with `countHeadSignals` — the same patterns the strips act on — and requires `{title: 1, social: 0, canonical: 0, jsonLd: 0}` plus exactly one robots directive, and its text states why the asymmetry is intended: a canonical here would point a crawler at the missing entity as though it were the page's home, and a JSON-LD node would be structured data about something that no longer exists.

- [x] **`stripStaleHeadSignals` removes a JSON-LD block by running its replace to a fixpoint, which can synthesise a match the input never contained.** The loop in `head_splice.ts` re-runs `replace` until the string stops changing, added to satisfy `js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization`. Deleting a span can splice the two sides together, so a second pass can match a `<script type="application/ld+json">…</script>` formed out of the wreckage of the first — the same hazard `document_title.test.ts` and `learn_structured_data.test.ts` both spell out in their own comments as the reason they consume HTML comments in ONE alternation rather than stripping them in a prior pass, and then chose the alternation instead. The two are inconsistent about the same risk. Nothing is broken: the input is our own build artifact, not attacker-controlled, and `head_splice.test.ts` pins the overlapping-open case the loop was written for. But the durable form is the one the two seo guards already use — a single alternation whose first branch consumes what must be skipped — and if that is adopted the CodeQL suppression the loop exists for has to be re-checked rather than assumed. Not taken here because it is a sanitiser rewrite with no observed defect behind it, and the round's budget went to the two strip/inject disagreements that DID have one. Owner tree: `apps/web/src/lib/share/head_splice.ts`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1192](../architecture/decisions.md)).** The loop was exploitable, and it was also unnecessary — both halves measured rather than argued. Unnecessary: a global replace consumes every leftmost non-overlapping match the input holds, and an open with any close after it always matches at that open, so after one pass the only opens left are ones with no close anywhere, which no number of passes removes either; over 500,000 generated documents a single pass never once left a matchable block, and the suite's own overlapping-opens case — the one the loop was written for — passes unchanged without it. Exploitable: put `<scr` before a real block and `ipt type="application/ld+json">` after it, and deleting the block joins them into an open whose nearest close is the SPA bundle's, so the second pass swallowed `</head>`, the mount div and the bundle tag and the splice then returned the shell unmeta'd — the exact § 1086 damage, from the mechanism added to prevent it, in all 48 documents of that family. Loop removed, case pinned, and the tree no longer disagrees with itself: the two seo guards' one-alternation rule and this module now say the same thing. **Amended the same day ([decisions § 1194](../architecture/decisions.md)): removing the loop was half the fix.** Running the whole share suite rather than the module's own file turned up a test in `share_route_spa_shell.test.ts` asserting the loop's behaviour was REQUIRED, and it was guarding something real — deleting a match to the EMPTY STRING joins the characters either side, so the output can be re-parsed into a JSON-LD element the input never held. Both forms were wrong: one synthesises a block, the other chases it and cannot stop. A match is now replaced by a newline, which a tag name cannot contain, so the join is prevented rather than arbitrated; applied to all four signals, since the hazard is general to delete-based rewriting. The two cases now bracket it from both sides.

Date().timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate`, so a blank interval falls back to the delivery instant and credits normally. `git log -S` puts that fallback in the same commit as the accumulator (#856) and this text one round later (#857). The residual routes to a run-long zero are not silent in the same way — a `mostRecentQuantity()` that never answers also leaves `currentBPM` at a dash on the wrist, and a declined Health read grant genuinely had a sensor delivering none of the time, which HealthKit gives an app no way to distinguish anyway. **The half that was true — it had never executed — is fixed at the root.** `HeartRateCoverageAccumulator` is a value type owning the credited total, the tick mark and the sample stamp, with `begin` / `reset` / `noteSample(atEpoch:)` / `advance(activeElapsedSeconds:nowEpoch:)`; `advance` takes the instant it is measured at instead of reading a clock, so a whole run walks through it in a millisecond. `HealthKitManager` delegates. Nine new cases in `HealthKitFailureTests` cover a sensor delivering throughout, one quitting at twenty minutes of an hour (1230 credited seconds of 3600, coverage 0.34, `avg_bpm` suppressed — the path the figure exists for), a late first sample, a silence charged once rather than re-credited, a repeated tick, a non-finite tick, and both unmeasured branches. **Rung: *host-tested*, and NOT above it.** No Swift compiler exists on this workstation or in Linux CI; the tests are written to run in the macOS `test-watch-ios` job and have not run anywhere yet. ### Surfaced by the #789 round 39 shared-rails lane (2026-09-05)

- [x] **`check_twin_claims.mjs` reads about three quarters of the twin claims in the tree, and its floor is set too low to notice.** Measured, and the root cause of [decisions § 1204](../architecture/decisions.md) — and, one level up, of why the § 641 class keeps recurring. Two mechanisms. **(1)** `headerComment` folds only the comment block at the very top of a file and breaks at the first non-comment line, so a file whose doc block sits after an `import` returns an EMPTY header: 27 files carry a twin-shaped claim naming an `apps/` path that the guard never sees at all, including `apps/web/src/lib/runs/run_stats.ts`, `runs/grade_adjusted_pace.ts`, `runs/age_grade.ts`, `runs/pace_analysis.ts`, `apps/mobile_android/lib/elevation.dart` and `lib/fitness.dart`. Fix: fold the first doc-comment BLOCK in the file rather than the block at offset zero — skip leading `import` / `library;` / blank lines before starting, or scan the first N lines and take the longest comment run. **(2)** Inside the headers it does read, `DECLARATION` wants a verb from a fixed list then a backticked path ending in `.ts`/`.dart`, and misses four forms found in the tree: `the Dart twin \`path\`` with no *of* (`training/hr_zones.ts`), `Mirrors apps/…/x.dart` with no backticks (`training/workout_kind_color.ts`), a backticked path with a `:symbol` suffix (`runs/run_stats.ts` names `…/run_stats.dart:movingTimeOf`), and `ported from \`path\`` (`training/goals.ts`). Widening for those four over the same headers finds 27 more declarations — 24 for already-registered pairs, two unregistered, one dangling. Suggested regex: add `(?:Dart|TS) twin` and `[Pp]orted from` and `[Dd]art port of` to the verb alternation, make the backticks optional, and allow a `(?::[A-Za-z0-9_]+)?` suffix after the extension. **(3)** `MIN_DECLARATIONS = 60` exists to catch exactly a scanner that stopped matching, but the census is 106, so it has 46 of slack and a 25 % shortfall passes it. Raise it with the widening, and keep it within ~10 of the real count. Owner tree: `scripts/check_twin_claims.mjs` + its `.test.mjs`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1243](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Both named mechanisms fixed and the floor raised to 155 with a test that fails when its slack under the real census exceeds 15. Census **106 -> 167**, none lost; the 37 empty-header files and the four unreadable declaration forms are all read now. Each of the three changes was mutation-tested by reverting it (2, 7 and 1 failing cases respectively). Two further forms are measured and re-filed below rather than fixed: a RELATIVELY-named counterpart (11 cross-platform instances) and a declaration sitting below the file's first statement.

Owner tree: `apps/web/` + a migration. **CLOSED (caller half) 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1232](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Every claim in this entry was checked and holds: no unique index, no per-day dedupe, the `{ error }` unbound, and `fetchFitnessSnapshots(60)` newest-first. The entry's proposed fix — "a per-(user, day) unique index plus an upsert" — is half wrong, and the measurement is worth keeping: `fitness_snapshots` has self SELECT / INSERT / DELETE policies and NO UPDATE one, so `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` is refused by RLS; and `on_conflict=` names columns, not expressions, so it cannot address a derived-day target at all. The caller therefore gates on a read of the newest `computed_at` plus a pure `fitnessSnapshotDue` (UTC day, fail-closed) and absorbs a 23505 on the insert — correct with no constraint, race-proof once one exists. The index half (`fitness_snapshots_user_day_uniq`) is the backend lane's. DDL half CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1235](../architecture/decisions.md#1235-one-fitness-snapshot-per-runner-per-day-and-the-append-only-shape-that-made-the-duplicates))**, migrations `20270710000001` + `20270710000002`. `fitness_snapshots_user_day_uniq` over `(user_id, snapshot_day)` — a stored `date` derived from `computed_at` by a BEFORE INSERT trigger and pinned on UPDATE. A stored column rather than an expression index because `timezone()` is STABLE (Postgres refuses the expression in an index and in a STORED generated column alike) and because PostgREST's `on_conflict` takes columns, never an expression or an index name. Existing duplicates are reduced first, batched per user, keeping the greatest `(computed_at, id)` per group — with the migration stating plainly that batching inside a wrapped file bounds the work per statement and not the lock (§ 1148). **An UPDATE policy ships with it**: the table was append-only, which only worked because every mount appended — enforce one row per day without an update path and the day's numbers freeze at the first mount. 15 pgtap assertions, 7 planted defects. The client half (read-then-insert with a 23505 absorb, or an upsert now that the UPDATE arm exists) is the `web-data` lane's. **Both halves are in one PR, so the sequencing note in the caller half is historical: the UPDATE policy the DDL half added means an upsert is now possible, and the read-then-insert path was written to be correct either way.**

### Surfaced by the #789 round 39 web-core lane, second wave (2026-09-05)

- [x] **`recap.dart` still anchors the current streak at 31 December, so the pair is diverged and a phone-published snapshot of an in-progress period carries a zero.** [§ 1221](../architecture/decisions.md). The web half is fixed; `apps/mobile_android/lib/recap.dart:345` is `final endOfYear = DateTime(year, 12, 31, 23, 59);` and `:483` `final endOfMonth = DateTime(year, month + 1, 0, 23, 59);`, each passed straight to `computeRunStreaks` as its `today` anchor. The change is the same shape as the web one and needs no new concepts: add a trailing optional `DateTime now = ...` to `buildYearInRunningRecap` (`:248`, currently `[RecapExtras extras = const RecapExtras()]`) and `buildMonthInRunningRecap` (`:408`), thread it through the month builder's own call to the year builder (`:414`), add the two-line `currentAnchor(periodEnd, now)` helper, and pass `currentAnchor(endOfYear, now)` / `currentAnchor(endOfMonth, now)`. Dart cannot default a parameter to `DateTime.now()` (it is not a compile-time constant), so make it `DateTime? now` and resolve `now ?? DateTime.now()` inside — that is the only shape difference from the TS side. Mirror the three new web tests into `apps/mobile_android/test/recap_test.dart` (the web suite is the reference), then run the iOS twin mirror. Mobile's `recapSnapshotJson` serialises `currentStreakDays` into `public_recaps`, so until this lands a snapshot published from a phone for the current year or month renders a zero on the web share page while the web-built one renders the real streak. Owner trees: `apps/mobile_android/` + `apps/mobile_ios/`. **Closed** by [§ 1239](../architecture/decisions.md): ported with the `DateTime? now` shape the entry describes, six mirrored cases (two of which the filing's own reasoning would have written wrong — see the ADR), all verified failing against the old anchor.

The consequence for the other reader is unchanged: a non-owner following a shared link to a run whose fundraiser read failed sees the section render nothing at all, exactly as if the runner had never created one. The component already models a *second* failure precisely (`totalsFailed`, so a totals blip is not shown as "0 raised"), which is the pattern to copy: add a `loadFailed` state, keep the owner-CTA fallback for the owner, and render a one-line retry for everyone else. Owner tree: `apps/web/`. **CLOSED 2026-09-05 ([decisions § 1231](../architecture/decisions.md)).** Taken exactly as prescribed — a `loadFailed` state, the owner-CTA fallback kept, a one-line `role="alert"` retry for everyone — plus the Playwright spec `tests-e2e/fundraising/section-load-failure.spec.ts` (written, NOT run in-lane), whose second case is the control the first needs: a run with genuinely no campaign must still render nothing. **This entry's stated blocker was wrong**: `fundraiser.loadFailed` and `fundraiser.retry` already exist in all seven catalogues (`/fundraisers/[id]` added them), so no new key was needed and the i18n-tree ownership was never the obstacle.

Every other join-shaped insert in the file swallows it. One-line, but it wants the same `23505`-is-idempotent treatment applied consistently rather than case by case. - [x] **A phone that has not updated can no longer write 465 exercise names rather than 410, until it does.** DECIDED: an honest doc note, not a client-visible mitigation — [§ 1252](../architecture/decisions.md), note landed in `docs/features/gym_programming.md`. Measured: of the 465, ZERO lie in Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended-A, Latin Extended-B, Cyrillic, Latin Extended Additional or Greek Extended, so reaching the refusal means naming a lift in Cherokee, Georgian Mtavruli, Deseret, Adlam, Garay, Medefaidrin, Vithkuqi or Sidetic on a pre-§ 1175 build. Stated as a measured consequence of [§ 1175](../architecture/decisions.md), not as a regression: the fold now WIDENS on the server at 55 code points, so a client build from before this change disagrees with the server's CHECK at 465 code points where it previously disagreed at 410. The reachable survivors are ranked and re-filed individually below; everything else is unreachable by measurement (handle match bounded by `^[a-z0-9_]{3,30}$`, certificate filename strips to `[A-Za-z0-9]` before folding, uuid hex, and ~20 machine-token folds). ### Surfaced by the #789 round 40 web-landing lane (2026-09-05)

- [ ] **The SPA shell's filename moved in the repo, and the live distribution has not been taken through the sequence that makes that safe.** [§ 1268](../architecture/decisions.md) renamed the shell from `index.html` to `200.html` across all three rails; [§ 1269](../architecture/decisions.md) states the three-step operator sequence that moves a LIVE distribution without a window where the 403 body is wrong — (1) `aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/index.html s3://<bucket>/200.html` while the two are byte-identical, (2) `terraform apply` the 403 to `/200.html`, (3) deploy the tag. **The repo change is merged and the sequence has never been executed**, so a deploy that skips step 1 or reorders it serves the prerendered landing page — broken, since its asset URLs resolve under the deep link's own directory ([§ 1270](../architecture/decisions.md)) — for every client route until the apply catches up. ### Surfaced by the #789 round 40 shared-rails lane (2026-09-05)

Resolving one means guessing a root; a suffix match against `SOURCE_ROOTS` resolves 11, but two of them are `settings_safety_screen.dart -> core/data.ts` and `password_change.ts -> settings_account_screen.dart` — claims about a screen and a 12,000-line data module, neither registrable — so widening buys two real pairs at the cost of four header rewords in other trees. The cheaper durable fix is the opposite direction: make the headers name repo-rooted paths (one was already fixed this round, `adaptive_fitness_flag.dart`) and leave the guard strict. **(2) A declaration below the file's first statement.** `headerComment` now steps over an import prologue but still stops at the first line of real code, which is right — a claim 300 lines down is not a header — but it means `adaptive_fitness_flag.dart`, whose module doc sits under a `const`, is read as having no header at all. Both are false NEGATIVES only: nothing the guard reports is wrong. Owner tree: `scripts/check_twin_claims.mjs` plus whichever trees hold the headers. **CLOSED in the round-41 guards lane** ([§ 1314](../architecture/decisions.md)) — both forms are read. The filing was wrong in both halves and in the same direction: the relative form buys ZERO new pairs from the header alone (all eleven resolve uniquely, six already registered, five unregistrable), and the below-the-statement form is not low-value, because **the two mechanisms intersect** — `off_route_flag.dart` and `weigh_in_flag.dart` are named relatively AND sit under a documented top-level `const`, so each was invisible twice over and both were live § 641-class pairs in neither registry ([§ 1315](../architecture/decisions.md)). The four header rewords the entry priced were avoided entirely: a claim the registries cannot carry now resolves to a `NOT_PAIRS` entry instead ([§ 1317](../architecture/decisions.md)). Census 167 → 190, floor 155 → 178.

The write side is untouched and was another lane's tree this round: `apps/web/src/routes/settings/account/+page.svelte:590` writes `parseInt(maxHr, 10) || null` with no bound at all, and the preferences page's `min="100" max="230"` is an advisory HTML attribute on a field that autosaves `onblur`, so neither refuses a 300. The module's export keeps its `SharedWorkoutSet[]` signature (`routes/share/workout/[id]/+page.svelte` imports it and is another lane's tree) and is now an adapter over `gym_prs`' canonical `distinctExerciseCount`, holding no fold of its own. The filing was right about the fold and understated the consequence. `hasExact` has always folded canonically while `filtered` did not, and the empty state renders on `filtered.length === 0 && !canCreate` — so an entry the naive filter cannot see but `hasExact` can find hides the list AND suppresses the create affordance. Simulated over the component's two derived expressions, three catalogue spellings reach that dead end (`Bench<U+00A0>Press`, `Bench  Press`, `İncline Press`, each queried with the ordinary spelling), and the entry that traps the picker is one a user can create in the same field. Folding both sides through `normaliseExerciseName` closes it structurally: an entry whose key equals the query's key necessarily contains it. The filing's note about the sort was followed — `localeCompare` stays, and the measured divergence is re-filed below against the mobile side. The `PENDING` entry is gone and the list is now empty on both platforms.

The durable fix for the whole stale-client class, and the pattern is already in the tree one column over: `gym_sets_stamp_exercise_key_trigger` (migration `20270706000001`) is a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger whose own comment says it "stamps unconditionally, so a client-supplied exercise_key is replaced rather than rejected". The other two columns instead carry a CHECK that REFUSES a disagreeing client value, which is what couples them to the client's Unicode version — 410 code points before [§ 1175](../architecture/decisions.md), 465 after, and 55 newly so. Extending the same trigger to both turns every version of that refusal into a silent correction and takes all three numbers to zero permanently; the CHECKs can stay as belt-and-braces since nothing would then be able to violate them. Needs a migration and a re-validate, so it belongs to whoever owns `apps/backend/`. Owner tree: `apps/backend/supabase/migrations/`. **CLOSED 2026-09-06** (migration `20270711000001`, [decisions § 1284](../architecture/decisions.md)). Both triggers landed with the same unqualified `before insert or update` shape and the same constant `''` default, so the two `Insert` types stop obliging a client to compute a key the server derives. **No re-validate was needed and that is a proof rather than a shortcut**: both CHECKs are already VALIDATED, which is a statement about every row, so the derivation held for all of them and a backfill would have touched nothing. The CHECKs stay — a correcting trigger makes them unviolatable rather than redundant, and they are what turns a lost trigger into a loud refusal; `exercise_key_server_stamped_test.sql` (11 tests) disables the trigger to prove that half is still live. The three head-inserting routines split three ways on this: `clone_plan_template` and `clone_public_plan` both write literal `null, null` with the comment "publisher-private fitness data — never propagated to the clone", `20260721_001` backs that with `private.strip_template_private_fields` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, nulls both columns on any `is_template` row) so a template cannot hold them at all — and `assign_plan_to_athlete` writes `src.vdot, src.current_5k_seconds` from a source plan that is NOT a template and therefore CAN hold them. So a coach assigning one of their own plans lands their own fitness numbers on a row the athlete owns and can read. Two defensible readings and the code states neither: either the paces are the coach's prescription and the VDOT they were derived from is part of the prescription (keep it, and say so in the migration), or it is the same publisher-private class the other two paths null and the strip trigger should not have been scoped to `is_template` (null it, and extend the trigger). The prescription reading was checked and does not hold: `plan_workouts` carries the prescription in full, `plan.vdot` renders as an unattributed "VDOT 52.3" header stat on five surfaces, and `current_5k_seconds` is a measurement of the coach under any reading. The strip trigger was deliberately **not** extended: RLS's `with check (auth.uid() = user_id …)` makes this RPC the only path that can create a row owned by somebody else, and a trigger keyed on `assigned_by_coach_id` would fire on every later update and delete the ATHLETE's own notes. `assign_plan_to_athlete_test.sql` goes 8 → 11, asserting at the assigned row (the source now holds all three, so the copy is observable) and pinning that `rules` still propagates.

### Surfaced by the #789 round 41 web-share-coach lane (2026-09-06)

Closing the last three `PENDING` entries in
`apps/web/src/lib/gym/exercise_key_source_guard.test.ts` emptied the list, and
emptying it made the guard's blind spot legible: it bans the WRONG fold and is
blind to NO fold. A scan of every web comparison of an `exercise_name` found
five sites in that second shape. Details in

### Surfaced by the #789 round 41 mobile-stores lane (2026-09-06)

- [ ] **`instance_start` is minted from the reader's timezone on mobile, and from the true instant on web.** Full trace + evidence in [decisions § 1291](../architecture/decisions.md). `recurrence.dart` sets `useUtc = e.timezone != null`, so a recurring event with no declared timezone gets occurrences built with the unnamed `DateTime(...)` constructor — a LOCAL instant. That reaches `api_client` as `EventView.nextInstanceStart`, and every one of its `instance_start` sites serialises with a bare `.toIso8601String()` (`rsvpToEvent`, the attendee read, `fetchEventResults`, `fetchRaceSession`, the run-photo query, `upsertCheckpointCrossing` — lines 3462 / 4911 / 4928 / 4972 / 5008 of `packages/api_client/lib/src/api_client.dart`), which writes no zone designator for a local `DateTime`. Postgres resolves the zone-less literal in the session's own TimeZone and matches `instance_start` with `=`, so two readers in different zones write two different keys for one occurrence. Web's `recurrence.ts` keeps the same `event.timezone` branch but a JS `Date` is an instant and `toISOString()` always emits `Z`, so web writes the true instant and a phone RSVP does not appear in the web attendee list for that occurrence. **Read-derived, not executed** — no run was made against a live occurrence; the precondition is recurring + `timezone` null + reader not at UTC. The durable fix is one change in one place: either `api_client` normalises every `instance_start` (all consumers move together) or `recurrence.dart` stops minting local instants. Fixing it in one store would be worse than leaving it — it would file that store's rows under a key no other surface writes, which is why `local_crossings_store.dart`'s site carries a `zone-verbatim:` marker instead. Owner tree: `packages/api_client/lib/src/api_client.dart` + `apps/mobile_android/lib/recurrence.dart` + the iOS twin (+ `apps/web/src/lib/social/recurrence.ts` if the parity pair moves).
- [ ] **`storedClockOrNow` falls back to `now`, which lets a corrupt clock freeze a synced row against the server forever.** [decisions § 1290](../architecture/decisions.md) made a wrong-typed `last_modified_at` behave like an absent one instead of discarding the whole record, and deliberately did not change the fallback VALUE. `now` is not obviously right: a `synced` row handed `now` wins `local.lastModifiedAt.isAfter(serverTs)` in every subsequent `replaceFromServer`, and `rewriteAll` persists that clock, so the row keeps winning across launches and the server can never overwrite it. The epoch (`DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0, isUtc: true)`) loses every newer-wins comparison while still keeping an unsynced row and still pushing it, which is right in both directions. The change is one line in `offline_sync_store.dart`, but it moves behaviour for the three inputs (absent / empty / unparseable) that already took `now` before this round, so it wants its own measurement of what actually reaches it. Owner tree: `apps/mobile_android/lib/offline_sync_store.dart` + the iOS twin.
- [ ] **`DateTime.tryParse` rolls out-of-range components over rather than refusing them, and three stores read a `date` column with it.** `2026-13-45T99:99:99Z` parses to 2027-02-18T04:40:39Z; `2026-06-32` parses to 2026-07-02. Pinned in `offline_sync_timestamps_test.dart` for `parseServerTimestamp`, whose callers only compare or store the result, so a confident wrong answer is harmless there. It is NOT obviously harmless for `local_gear_store.dart`'s `_parseDate`, which feeds `purchasedAt` / `retiredAt` into `api.createGear` / `api.updateGear` and therefore writes the rolled-over day back to a `date` column. Nothing produces such a value today (the mobile date picker cannot), so this is a robustness gap rather than a live defect. Owner tree: `apps/mobile_android/lib/local_gear_store.dart` + the iOS twin.

### Surfaced by the #789 round 41 infra-ci lane (2026-09-06)

- [x] **CodeQL analysed one of this repo's two Go modules, and the explicit build was what turned off the fallback that would have caught the other.** Closed 2026-09-06 ([decisions § 1304](../architecture/decisions.md)). `security.yml`'s `codeql-go` job had one build step — `go build ./...` in `apps/job_worker` — under a comment reading "Our only Go module is apps/job_worker". `apps/graph_cycle` has been a second module since the route-loop sidecar landed: its own `go.mod`, 27 source files, a `Test graph_cycle sidecar (Go)` job in `ci.yml`, a `release-graph-cycle.yml`, and a Trivy job **in the same file** that builds its image — so its dependencies were scanned and its source never was, on a service that terminates HTTP. Go has no build-less extraction ("CodeQL will analyze whatever source code is built by your specified build steps"), so the set of modules built is the set scanned, and a database holding one module's code looks no different from one holding two. **The single build was also what suppressed the safety net**, which is why this survived: `analyze-action.ts` at the pinned SHA carries `runAutobuildIfLegacyGoWorkflow`, which walks every module, and skips when "at least one file of Go code has already been extracted" — which building `job_worker` guarantees. Had the step never been added, both modules would have been scanned. Fixed by enumerating `go.mod` directories from the tree rather than listing them, so a third module is scanned the day it lands, with a population floor of two so a `find` that stopped matching fails instead of going green having scanned nothing (mutation-tested: pointing `find` at a name nothing matches refuses at `COUNT=0`). Both modules build clean; `actionlint` and all six workflow/infra guards pass.

- [x] **Three comments on the CloudFront 403 block were false, two of them contradicting the same block they sit in.** Closed 2026-09-06 ([decisions § 1308](../architecture/decisions.md)). The block's opening line still read "SPA fallback — SvelteKit static fallback is index.html" while the paragraph 30 lines below states the shell is `/200.html` and the resource sets exactly that. A second sentence described the distribution rewriting "a 404 to the shell at 404" — a mapping [§ 1022](../architecture/decisions.md) added and [§ 1084](../architecture/decisions.md) removed — contradicting the block six lines beneath it that explains why no 404 mapping exists. The irony is on the record: that same paragraph congratulates itself for resolving an earlier pair of contradictory comments in this very file ("Two comments in one file cannot both be true; this is the one that was wrong") and had since acquired two more. `terraform validate` has no opinion about comments, `fmt` does not read them, and `check_infra_error_responses.mjs` parses `error_code` and `response_page_path` rather than prose — so nothing read these, which is the general form of the problem. The replacements name the mechanism and cite the ADR that owns it, and the deploy-order note now also points at `docs/ops/deployment.md` so the runbook and the resource that needs it are one link apart.

- [ ] **CodeQL's Kotlin leg claimed `apps/mobile_android/android` and never reached it — 11 platform-channel bridges are unscanned, including a `BroadcastReceiver`.** Same defect class as [§ 1304](../architecture/decisions.md)'s Go one, found by looking for it once the Go leg was understood, and the reason it is filed rather than fixed in the same change is cost. `security.yml`'s `codeql-kotlin` job has exactly one build step, `./gradlew compileDebugKotlin` in `apps/watch_wear/android`; CodeQL analyses what the build steps compile; and the `runAutobuildIfLegacyGoWorkflow` fallback that had been quietly covering the Go side is Go-specific with no Java/Kotlin analogue. So the 128 Kotlin/Java files under `apps/watch_wear` are analysed and the 11 under `apps/mobile_android/android` are not — `MainActivity.kt`, `RunActionReceiver.kt` (a `BroadcastReceiver`, a classic Android attack surface), `HealthRoutePermissionBridge.kt`, `CalendarBridge.kt`, `BatterySettingsBridge.kt` among them. These are the platform-channel bridges that mediate health permissions, calendar access and foreground-service actions, which is exactly the code Java/Kotlin queries are for. **The fix is not another build line**: the Flutter host's Gradle build needs the pinned Flutter SDK set up in this job (`local.properties`, the generated plugin registrant), so it means adding a Flutter setup step to a CodeQL job and paying its minutes on every PR and every weekly cron. That is a real trade to weigh, not an oversight to sweep up at the tail of a round. The header comment now states the gap instead of claiming the coverage, so whoever takes this starts from the truth. Owner tree: `.github/workflows/security.yml`.

The next round should run `init -backend=false` + `validate` in `infra/bootstrap`, `infra/dns`, `infra/github-oidc`, `infra/envs/prod` and `infra/envs/preview`, plus `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra`, and plant one undeclared-variable reference in the module to confirm the transitive path still reports. Note what this class of check structurally cannot see — round 41's own three false comments passed `validate` and `fmt` without a murmur. Owner tree: `infra/`.

- [ ] **`POST /api/coach/turn` answered 200 text/html on prod, and the coach path's own statuses say that means the Lambda was never reached.** Split out of the distribution-wide-403 entry above, because that entry is a design question that will stay open and this is a possible live outage that should not wait behind it. The measurement is round 34's, on prod 2026-09-05, and is not disputed; the attribution was. `apps/web/src/lib/coach/handler.ts` returns **401** for an unauthenticated call at two separate exits, nothing on this distribution maps 401, and the only 403 the coach path emits is the AI-disclosure consent refusal — which needs an authenticated caller with a profile row and is unreachable by the request that was measured. The cache behaviour is not the explanation either: `/api/coach*` has its own `ordered_cache_behavior` targeting `lambda-coach` with `POST` in `allowed_methods`. So the 200 text/html was not a coach 403 being rewritten. Three things produce that reading and all three are bad: the request never reaching the Lambda (the issue #590 shape `main.tf` records as proven once — one of the two OAC grants missing, the Function URL 403ing *before invocation*, the mapping rewriting it to the shell at 200, "the surface reads healthy while the Lambda never runs"), a stale prod bundle, or a prod `/api/coach*` behaviour that does not match the repo. **Neither coach alarm can see any of them**: `-coach-lambda-errors` and `-coach-lambda-p95` key on Lambda `Errors` and `Duration`, which a request that is never invoked does not emit — the § 890 invisible-failure class, in the one place the module's own comment warns about it. **The check needs no credentials**: an unauthenticated `POST https://threkir.com/api/coach/turn` that reaches the Lambda answers 401 with a JSON body, so anything else is proof it did not, independently of the mapping. One `curl`. If it does answer 401 today, the round-34 reading was a transient or a since-fixed deploy and this closes; if it answers 200 text/html, the coach endpoint is down and has been since at least 2026-09-05. Not run by this lane, which is forbidden from touching the production distribution. Owner: anyone who can issue that request, then whoever holds prod credentials. [decisions § 1307](../architecture/decisions.md).

So it is absent from `unmeasuredCases` (which filters `ran`) and from `phantomKills` unless a mutation happens to name it — and a case nobody wrote a mutation for is exactly the case nobody names. The guard's own header had claimed the stronger rule ("a new case fails this guard until a mutation names it") that these two edges could not deliver. Closed with a static, host-free source census (`declaredCases` + `unnamedDeclaredCases` + `staleExemptions`, the § 1273 declared-exemption shape): with `ran ⊆ kills`, `kills ⊆ ran` and `declared ⊆ kills` the three sets are one, and all four quadrants are covered. **The class has exactly one instance in the repo**, ruled out by measurement: `ignore:` appears in no other of the 70 `*.test.ts` files under `supabase/functions/`, nothing else registers a `Deno.test` inside a conditional, every test file declares at least one case, and the only test-shaped non-`*.test.ts` file is a production module.

'<literal>'` reads as a dead branch and was first written up here as one; measured (`FOO= deno eval 'Deno.env.get("FOO")'` → `""`, a string), `??` coalesces only on `undefined`, so an ABSENT secret ran the case and an EMPTY one skipped it. Empty is what a `SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET:` line with nothing after the colon produces, two lines from a `SENTRY_DSN=` in the same `.env.local` heredoc. ### Surfaced by the #789 round 41 watch lane (2026-09-06)

- [ ] **A permanently-rejected run keeps the queue non-empty forever, and there is no surface that says so or lets the runner clear it.** `drainQueueLoop` classifies a 400/404/409/422 as `SkipAndContinue`, leaves the entry in the queue, and its own comment says "the run stays in the queue until the user manually discards it from the UI". Two things make that untrue. **(1)** `lastError = null` runs on every successful push, so any later success in the same pass erases the skipped run's message; `anyTransientFailure` stays false, the caller runs `drainBackoff.onSuccess()` and sets `syncError = null`. Every Sync tap therefore reports success while the queue count never falls. **(2)** The discard the comment points at is `RunViewModel.discard()`, which acts on `state.thisRunId` — the run just finished, on the PostRun screen. Once the runner leaves that screen a stuck entry has no discard affordance at all. **Filed rather than changed, deliberately.** The `lastError` behaviour is not an oversight: `DrainQueueLoopTest` asserts it twice, in terms ("Skip-followed-by-success clears the banner", "Trailing success clears the banner even if a middle run was skipped"), so flipping it is reversing a stated decision, not fixing a slip. And flipping it alone would surface a message the runner can act on in exactly no way — the useful remedy is a queue-management surface the watch does not have, which [§ 24](../architecture/decisions.md#24-web-is-the-canonical-feature-surface-mobile-and-watches-are-platform-additive) says is not a thing to invent on the wrist without an owner decision. What is owed is that decision: either the wrist gets a "1 run can't sync — discard?" affordance and `lastError` is retained for skipped entries, or the entry is auto-dropped after N failed passes with the reason logged. Verified by reading only; nothing here was run against a watch.

- [ ] **`metadata.hr_coverage` from `apps/watch_ios` has still never been produced by a real `HKWorkoutSession`.** Re-filed from the round-38/39 entry above, narrowed to exactly the part [§ 1299](../architecture/decisions.md) does not discharge. The accumulator is now *host-tested* — nine cases walk whole runs through `HeartRateCoverageAccumulator` — but host-tested is two rungs below what this figure needs before any doc may call it verified, and the tests themselves have not run anywhere yet either: no Swift compiler exists on this workstation or in Linux CI, and the macOS `test-watch-ios` job is the only machine that will ever see them. What is owed is unchanged: one recorded run on a simulator or a paired watch, `hr_coverage` present on the row and plausibly non-zero, per the *bench-verified* rung in [`docs/custom_watch/quality_standards.md`](../custom_watch/quality_standards.md). `metadata.md` and § 1207 both already say no doc may describe the figure as verified until then. Owner: whoever next has a Mac and a paired watch.

- [ ] **The two watch clients' heart-rate coverage helpers are a parity pair in meaning and in nothing else.** `HeartRateCoverage` (Swift) and `HeartRateCoverage.kt` (Kotlin) write the same `runs.metadata.hr_coverage` column, share the 0.5 suppression threshold and the 30 s freshness window by hand, and say so in each other's doc comments — but they are in neither parity registry, `check_parity_pair_registry.mjs` cannot see them, and the `shared-library-syncer` agent's table does not carry them. That is [§ 641](../architecture/decisions.md)'s shape exactly: a declared lockstep nothing can detect a divergence in. The registries pair web with mobile and the two watch clients are additive surfaces under § 24, so the answer is probably a third rail in `scripts/check_shared_constants.mjs` — which already compares figures across non-registry rails — reading `minAverageBPMCoverage` / `MIN_AVG_BPM_COVERAGE` and `sampleFreshInterval` / `HR_SAMPLE_FRESH_MS` out of both files and failing on disagreement. Not taken in-round: `scripts/check_shared_constants.mjs` is shared with every other lane, and the round-41 watch lane already touched one shared script. Small and mechanical once owned.
